title: --incomplete overrides a fail verdict and any threshold
detail: decide() returns abstain for any receipt marked incomplete before it looks at the verdict or counts. Reproduced: `receipt --verdict fail --high 3 --threshold high --incomplete`, then `check --threshold high`, gives decision abstain. A review that already found blocking issues stops blocking as soon as one category was skipped, and the w-review closing step tells the agent to add --incomplete in exactly that case. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/push-gate.js:73.
fix_hint: Check failsThreshold() first and block on a fail verdict or findings at or above the threshold even when the receipt is incomplete; abstain on incomplete only when the recorded findings would not block.

title: Change id covers uncommitted edits, which a push does not send
detail: The id hashes HEAD's tree plus the uncommitted diff and the untracked files. A review run over uncommitted fixes records a receipt for HEAD+fixes. If the developer then pushes without committing those fixes, check sees the same dirty id and abstains, even though the pushed commits (HEAD only) were never reviewed in that form. That is a wrong pass for the input the gate exists to judge. Same code at .claude/helpers/kit/push-gate.js:256.
fix_hint: For check, key on what is pushed (base + HEAD tree) and treat a dirty tree as unreviewed, or have check refuse to abstain while the tree is dirty.

title: Documented receipt command never sets --threshold, so a threshold check always denies
detail: The closing step records receipts without --threshold, so every receipt is stored under 'none'. decide() blocks whenever the receipt's threshold differs from the check's (push-gate.js:274), so `check --threshold high|medium|low` denies even a 0/0/0 pass. Its message says to run /w-review again, and that writes the same 'none' receipt, so the user can never clear it. The threshold feature cannot be used through the workflow that is meant to feed it. The same text is in src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js:2260.
fix_hint: Add `[--threshold <level>]` to the closing-step command and say the check must use the same level. Or store counts without a threshold and judge them against the threshold given at check time.

title: Unknown flags are silently accepted
detail: parse() stores any --key value. A typo such as `check --treshold high` is ignored, so the check falls back to threshold none and gives 'ask' where a 'deny' (exit 2) was intended, with no error.
fix_hint: Allow only known flags for each subcommand (receipt: verdict/high/medium/low/threshold/incomplete/base; check: threshold/base) and throw KitExit 1 on any other flag.

title: Regenerated command file now holds literal backslash-escaped backticks
detail: Regenerating from the dot-shortcuts template wrote `\`` sequences into the markdown (lines 96, 100, 112, 115, 125 and the RC-A block at 144/152). The RC-A example is therefore no longer a fenced code block, and inline commands are no longer code spans. The regeneration also changed the build-phase browser check (it dropped 'Verify responsive layout, dark mode, accessibility'), which is outside this stream's scope.
fix_hint: Fix the over-escaped `\\\`` in the w-review template in src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js, then regenerate. Or limit this commit to the closing-step hunk.

title: Closing-step command contains a literal `pass|fail`
detail: If the command is pasted or run as written, the shell reads `pass|fail` as a pipe into a `fail` command and the receipt is not recorded. The placeholders `<H>` are also shell redirections. The same text is in src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js:2258.
fix_hint: Show two concrete forms (`--verdict pass` / `--verdict fail`) or write the placeholders as `VERDICT`, `H`, `M`, `L` in prose.

title: Weak or dead assertions in the receipt-history tests
detail: 'keeps the previous change ids' only checks that previous is an array; it never checks that an earlier id was pushed, deduplicated or capped at MAX_PREVIOUS. The unused `receipts`/`void receipts` (809, 816) and the `f`/`other` placeholders in the corrupt-store test (794-799) are dead code.
fix_hint: Check that previous contains the earlier change id, excludes the latest, and is capped at 50; remove the unused variables.

title: Store path is wrong when run from a subdirectory: receipt/check fail with a raw ENOENT or read the wrong store
detail: storeFile() resolves `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` against --show-toplevel, but git prints that path relative to the cwd (from <repo>/sub it prints '../.git'). Resolving it against the toplevel gives <parent>/.git. I reproduced this: `push-gate check` run from a subdirectory exits 1 with 'kit: ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath /tmp/pgt/.git'. That is an uncaught non-KitExit error with a misleading message, so neither receipt nor check works from any subdirectory. If the parent directory happens to have a .git, the gate keys a different store: a receipt recorded at the repo root is then reported as 'no review recorded' from the subdirectory (also reproduced). Mirrored at .claude/helpers/kit/push-gate.js:158. No test covers running from a subdirectory.
fix_hint: Use `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`, as workingTree() already does for --git-path, or resolve the path against the cwd instead of the toplevel. Add a test that records a receipt at the root and runs check from a subdirectory.

title: A missing or unspawnable git is reported as 'not inside a git repository'
detail: defaultGit maps a spawn failure (r.error set, status null, for example ENOENT when git is not on PATH) to code 1 with empty stderr and drops r.error. changeId's first probe then throws 'not inside a git repository', which sends the user the wrong way. Mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/push-gate.js.
fix_hint: When r.error is set, return or throw its message (for example, KitExit(`cannot run git: ${r.error.message}`)).

title: Receipt store update is an unlocked read-modify-write, and a failed write leaks its temp file
detail: run() reads the state, builds `previous`, then writeAtomic renames over the file. Two receipts recorded concurrently in the same repository (for example, two worktrees sharing the common dir, which hash to the same store) lose one writer's latest/previous entries. Separately, if writeFile or rename throws, the `<file>.<pid>.<rand>.tmp` file stays in the receipts dir, and the raw fs error surfaces instead of a KitExit.
fix_hint: Unlink the tmp file in a catch/finally and wrap the error in KitExit. Optionally take a lockfile (O_EXCL) around the read-modify-write.

title: Closing step requires a matching --threshold but not a matching --base
detail: The change id hashes the base. A receipt recorded without --base (merge-base with upstream, or root) and a check run with --base, or the reverse, never match. The check then reports 'only an earlier review exists, for a different version of this change', which misdescribes the situation and tells the user to re-run /w-review. The closing step only says to keep --threshold the same. Same text in src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js:2262.
fix_hint: Say to pass the same --base (or none) to both receipt and check, or record the base in the receipt and report a base mismatch distinctly in decide().

title: --path-format=absolute (git >= 2.31) silently misbehaves on older git
detail: workingTree (line 215) and storeFile (line 314) call `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute ...`. Git before 2.31 (Ubuntu 20.04 ships 2.25, Debian 11 2.30, RHEL 8 2.27-2.31) does not know the option; rev-parse passes unknown flags through to stdout and exits 0 (verified: `git rev-parse --bogus=absolute --git-common-dir` prints `--bogus=absolute\n<path>`, rc 0). So `must()` returns a two-line string. In workingTree the index copy then fails with ENOENT, which line 219 swallows, so `git add -u` runs on an empty temp index and write-tree returns the empty tree: a dirty receipt would hash the wrong tree. storeFile then calls fs.realpath on the two-line string and every receipt and check exits 1 with a cryptic `ENOENT ... realpath '--path-format=absolute\n...'`. The gate is unusable on these hosts and the error does not say why. No test covers older git or a minimum version.
fix_hint: Drop --path-format and resolve the relative output of `--git-common-dir` / `--git-path index` with path.resolve against `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`'s cwd (or the cwd git ran in), or check `git --version` and throw a clear KitExit for < 2.31; do not swallow ENOENT on the index copy when status reported changes.

title: Stale-lock check compares local clock to filesystem mtime
detail: withLock treats the lock as stale when Date.now() - st.mtimeMs > staleMs. When the receipts dir lives on a network home directory (NFS/SMB), mtime comes from the server clock; with more than 30s of skew a live lock can be taken over, or a dead one never treated as stale until waitMs expires. Two concurrent receipts can then lose a `previous` entry.
fix_hint: Write the owner pid and a local timestamp into the lock file and judge staleness from that content (or from the pid being dead) instead of the server-set mtime.

title: Secrets-file lines keep surrounding whitespace, so a padded entry never matches
detail: parseSecretsFile strips only a trailing \r and pushes the line as is. A secrets file line like 'tok-abcdef  ' (trailing spaces from an editor or paste) becomes the secret 'tok-abcdef  ', and redactSecrets('x tok-abcdef y', ...) returns replaced: 0, so the value goes out unredacted with no warning. The same applies to fingerprints (the hash covers the spaces). Multi-line blocks already get trimmed lines as candidates; single-line entries do not.
fix_hint: Trim single-line entries (secrets.push(line.trim())) before applying MIN_LENGTH, and add a test with a padded entry.

title: Default secrets file is not found from a linked git worktree, so redaction silently does nothing
detail: The default path is `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`/.claude/kit/secrets. In a linked worktree (the isolation marathon streams use), show-toplevel returns the worktree root. The secrets file is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. readFileOr(..., optional=true) returns null, and `redact` passes stdin through with replaced: 0 and no note. A user scrubbing text from inside a worktree gets back unredacted text that looks scrubbed.
fix_hint: Locate the main checkout through `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` (its parent directory) and use that as a fallback, or report in the output that no secrets file was found.

title: loadProjectSecrets doc says [] but the function returns null; nothing calls it
detail: The JSDoc says it returns [] when the file does not exist, but the code returns null. Nothing in the diff calls it: marathon's redactForModel parses the file on its own.
fix_hint: Return [] to match the doc, or fix the doc, or remove the unused export.

title: Secrets file that exists but cannot be reached is treated as 'no secrets' and fails open silently
detail: redactForModel gates on fileExists(), which returns false for any fs.access error, not only for a missing file. A dangling symlink (for example .claude/kit/secrets linked to a password store that is not mounted), EACCES on .claude/kit, or ELOOP all make review-brief skip redaction with no note, so the unredacted diff goes to the model and the brief says nothing. The kit CLI does the same: readFileOr treats ENOENT from a dangling symlink as 'missing default file' (verified: a dangling .claude/kit/secrets symlink gives {replaced: 0}, exit 0). The module promises the review-brief path fails closed on a broken secrets file, but these failures fail open.
fix_hint: Use fs.lstat (or check only e.code === 'ENOENT' on lstat) so 'the path exists in any form' blocks the brief; any other error, or a symlink whose target is missing, should stop with an error naming the path. In redact.js readFileOr, lstat before treating ENOENT as optional.

title: Secrets file present but kit missing: the diff goes out unredacted
detail: When .claude/kit/secrets exists, the user has said which values must not leave the machine. If the redact module cannot be imported (kit not installed, uninstalled, or redact.js/kit-exit.js missing, which the message check also swallows because the importer path contains 'redact.js'), review-brief still prints the whole raw diff and only adds a note at the end of the scope line. That note is easy to miss, and the secret has already gone out. The test locks in this fail-open behaviour instead of the fail-closed behaviour used for a malformed file.
fix_hint: When the secrets file exists and the redact module cannot load, fail the brief (or use a minimal inline exact-match redaction) rather than emit the unredacted diff; keep the 'works without kit' path only for when there is no secrets file.

title: Any git rev-parse failure is reported as 'not inside a git repository'
detail: secretsRoots maps every non-zero exit to 'not inside a git repository'. git older than 2.31 rejects --path-format=absolute, and running from inside .git rejects --show-toplevel. Both cases print a wrong diagnosis even though the user is in a repository.
fix_hint: Include a short, value-free summary of r.stderr in the message, or check for the specific 'not a git repository' text before using that wording.

title: Git older than 2.31 does not reject --path-format: it echoes it, and redaction silently fails open
detail: The new non-zero-status branch (lines 129-133, mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/redact.js) assumes git versions without --path-format fail with 'error: unknown option'. Real git rev-parse before 2.31 (Ubuntu 20.04 has 2.25, Debian 11 has 2.30, RHEL 8 ships 2.2x) does not do that. It passes unknown dash-arguments through show_flag, so it prints '--path-format=absolute' as its first output line and exits 0. secretsRoots then returns top='--path-format=absolute' (common is the toplevel path, whose basename is not .git). run() reads '--path-format=absolute/.claude/kit/secrets', resolved against process.cwd(), gets ENOENT, and readFileOr treats that as 'no secrets file'. The result is zero secrets and stdin passed through unredacted with exit 0. So on exactly the older environments the new diagnostic is meant for, the command leaks every secret instead of failing closed.
fix_hint: After a zero-status run, check that the output has exactly two lines and that both are absolute paths (path.isAbsolute(top) && !top.startsWith('-')). Otherwise throw a KitExit such as 'git >= 2.31 required (rev-parse --path-format); pass --secrets-file'. You could instead drop --path-format and resolve --show-toplevel and --git-common-dir against cwd yourself.

title: Old-git test fakes a stderr that real old git never produces
detail: The test stubs spawn to return status 128 with 'error: unknown option `path-format=absolute''. Real pre-2.31 git exits 0 and echoes the flag on stdout. The test therefore certifies a code path that never runs on old git, and it does not cover the fail-open case. It passes while the behaviour it names is wrong.
fix_hint:
Add a case with stub output { status: 0, stdout: '--path-format=absolute
/repo
.git
' } and assert that secretsRoots throws a KitExit and does not return a relative root.

title: 'all git versions print these relative to cwd' is not true for git < 2.13
detail: Before git 2.13, running rev-parse --git-common-dir and --git-path in a subdirectory printed the path relative to the top of the work tree, not to the cwd. Resolving that against cwd gives <sub>/.git. In push-gate the realpath or index copy then fails with a misleading error. In secretsRoots it adds a spurious extra root (<sub>). Both fail closed or are harmless, so no secret leaks, but the comment overstates what the code guarantees. The old-git test fake wraps modern git, so it cannot catch this.
fix_hint: Narrow the comment to git >= 2.13, or resolve the relative common-dir/git-path lines against --show-toplevel when the cwd-resolved path does not exist.

title: storeFile gets an undefined cwd when io.git has no .cwd and io.cwd is unset
detail: run() passes `git.cwd || io.cwd` to storeFile. changeId falls back to process.cwd() through its default parameter, but storeFile has no fallback, so gitPaths calls path.resolve(undefined, line) and throws a TypeError instead of a KitExit. This affects only programmatic callers, because the CLI always sets io.cwd.
fix_hint: Use `git.cwd || io.cwd || process.cwd()` in run() (or default the cwd parameter in storeFile/gitPaths).

title: rev-parse output error gives no next step and drops the caller's context
detail: When rev-parse exits 0 with odd output, resolveRevParse throws 'unexpected git rev-parse output (got N line(s), wanted M; first: ...)'. The `what` label gitPaths was given ('cannot find the index' / 'cannot find the git dir') is used only on a non-zero exit, and secretsRoots does not add its usual 'pass --secrets-file' remedy here. A user of redact or push-gate sees git internals with no action to take, unlike the neighbouring messages that name a fix.
fix_hint: Let the callers wrap or prefix the error: gitPaths prepends `what`, and secretsRoots appends '; pass --secrets-file' (optionally with a hint to check the git version).

title: Malformed-secrets failure is the only fail-closed message with no remedy
detail: The other new review-brief failures say 'refusing to emit an unredacted diff' and/or what to do (install the kit plugin or remove the secrets file). The malformed case says only '<rel> is malformed (<parser message>)'. The user is not told the brief was withheld on purpose or that fixing the file (for example closing the -----BEGIN block) unblocks it.
fix_hint: Use the same wording as the siblings: append ' — fix the file or remove it; refusing to emit an unredacted diff'.

title: A dangling secrets symlink is reported as a bare ENOENT
detail: This change deliberately treats a dangling symlink at the secrets path as an error. Yet redact reports 'cannot read secrets file <path>: ENOENT', and marathon (cli.js:705) reports 'cannot read .claude/kit/secrets (ENOENT)'. 'No such file' about a path the user can see with ls is confusing, and neither message says that the symlink target is missing or what to do (mount or restore the target, or remove the link).
fix_hint: When lstat succeeds but readFile gives ENOENT, say '<path> is a symlink to a missing target (<readlink>); restore it or remove the link'.

title: Lens step feeds `git diff HEAD`, which misses committed branch/PR work and untracked files
detail: /w-review is invoked as `/w-review [PR number or description]`, but the lens step always runs `git diff HEAD > /tmp/w-review.diff`. When the change under review is already committed (a PR or branch: the normal case), that diff is empty; brand-new files that are not yet `git add`ed are also left out. Traced in a temp repo: after committing a change that adds `await fetch(u)` to src/a.js and an `it(...)` test, `git diff HEAD | lenses --diff -` returns changed_files 0, fired [] and exit 0, so the reviewer records 'no lens applies' for a change that should fire missing-await and test-asserts-nothing. Same text is in src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js (~line 2121).
fix_hint: Diff against the review base, e.g. `git diff $(git merge-base HEAD <base>)` (or `gh pr diff <N>` for a PR number), and include untracked files (`git add -N` or `git diff --no-index`); tell the reviewer to treat changed_files 0 as 'wrong input', not 'no findings'. Update the test regex in test/w-review-command.test.js to match.

title: Diff paths keep `c/`/`i/`/`w/` prefixes under diff.mnemonicPrefix, so directory-anchored globs silently miss
detail: The `diff --git` regex only recognises `a/` and `b/`, and cleanPath only strips `[ab]/`. The w-review step runs a bare `git diff HEAD`, which honours the user's diff.mnemonicPrefix (or diff.srcPrefix/dstPrefix) config. Traced: with `git -c diff.mnemonicPrefix=true diff HEAD | lenses --diff -` the reported files are `w/src/a.js` and `w/test/b.test.js`. Any glob containing a `/` is anchored at the root (`test/**/*.js`, `src/**/*.ts`, typical project lenses), so it never matches `w/test/...` and the lens silently does not fire, with exit 0. (Only basename globs like `**/*.js` survive.)
fix_hint: Pin the prefixes where the diff is produced (`git diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ ...` in w-review.md and dot-shortcuts.js), and/or have the parser derive the path from the `+++`/`---` lines after stripping a single `[a-z]/` prefix that matches the diff --git header. Add a parseDiff test with mnemonic prefixes.

title: Empty or non-diff input is indistinguishable from 'no lens applies'
detail: If `--diff -` is run without a pipe (cli.js readStdin returns '' on a TTY), or `--diff` points at an empty or non-diff file, run() returns changed_files 0, fired [] and exits 0. Traced: `lenses --diff - < /dev/null` gives exit 0 with an empty result. A reviewer who mistypes the input or pipes the wrong thing gets a clean-looking 'nothing fired' instead of an error.
fix_hint: Fail with KitExit 1 when the input is non-empty but parses to zero files, and refuse `--diff -` when stdin is a TTY; or at minimum document in w-review that changed_files 0 means the input was wrong.

title: --no-prefix rename involving a single-letter directory loses that directory from the path
detail: The /w-review step produces the diff with --no-prefix. For a rename (or copy), the header halves differ, so the 'none' check at line 219 fails and the regex at line 221 is tried. That regex treats any leading '[a-z]/' as a git prefix. I reproduced it: renaming c/x.js to c/y.js with an edit gives 'diff --git c/x.js c/y.js' and '+++ c/y.js'. parseDiff takes mode 'git', and cleanPath then strips GIT_PREFIX, so the file is reported as 'y.js' when it should be 'c/y.js'. A rename from src/x.js to a/x.js goes the loose route and also comes out as 'x.js'. Any lens whose globs name a directory (for example 'c/**/*.js', or the test-asserts-nothing glob 'test/**' when the directory is t/) then silently fails to fire, and fired.files gives the reviewer the wrong path.
fix_hint: Treat a header as git-prefixed only when the halves use the expected prefix pairs (a/ b/, i/ w/, c/ w/, c/ o/, w/ w/...), not any [a-z]/. Better, read the path from the 'rename to' / 'copy to' lines (or from '+++' as given, with no stripping) when the header mode is uncertain. Add a test for a --no-prefix rename inside a one-letter directory.

title: Lens step writes the reviewed diff to one fixed shared path, /tmp/w-review.diff
detail: Every /w-review run, in every worktree and repo on the machine, writes to and reads back /tmp/w-review.diff. Marathon streams review several worktrees at once. If two reviews overlap, one review's 'node ... lenses --diff /tmp/w-review.diff' can read the other worktree's diff. It then fires lenses, and lists files, for a change it is not reviewing, or skips lenses that apply. Nothing reports an error, because the file is a valid diff, so the 'fix the range' safeguard never triggers.
fix_hint: Use a unique temp file per run (DIFF=$(mktemp) ... --diff "$DIFF"), or pipe straight in: '{ ...; } | node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js lenses --diff -'. Update the copy in .claude/commands/.shortcuts/w-review.md to match.

title: Trailing `; rm -f "$D"` masks the lens verb's non-zero exit
detail: The new snippet runs `node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js lenses --diff "$D"; rm -f "$D"`, so the block's exit status is rm's (0), never node's. The very next paragraph tells the agent that an empty/non-diff input exits 1 and that 'A non-zero exit means a lens file is broken: report it, do not skip the step'. Traced: with an empty $D (empty range, or mktemp failing on a read-only/full /tmp in an older or constrained environment so `> ""` fails and --diff "" resolves to the cwd), the CLI prints 'kit: no diff was given ...' to stderr and the Bash tool reports exit=0. Same for a broken lens file. The agent's exit-code-based check is silently defeated; the stderr text also names a temp path that has already been deleted. The same text is in src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js:2125 and test/w-review-command.test.js:53 asserts this exact masking form.
fix_hint: Preserve the status: `node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js lenses --diff "$D"; s=$?; rm -f "$D"; (exit $s)` (or a `trap 'rm -f "$D"' EXIT` before running node), mirror it in dot-shortcuts.js, and update the w-review-command test regex to require the preserved status.

title: Unindented '- item' list is refused with an error that says that form is supported
detail: The list-item regex on line 123 (/^\s+-\s+/) requires leading whitespace, but YAML commonly writes list items at column 0 under the key ("globs:\n- \"*.js\""). For that input parseLens throws 'f.md:4: cannot read this line (supported: "key: value", "key: [a, b]", "key:" then "- item" lines): - "*.js"'. The message tells the author that the exact form they wrote is supported, so they cannot tell what to change. The header comment ('or one `- item` per line') does not mention indentation either. Verified with parseLens. The same code is in src/lib/kit/lenses.js.
fix_hint: Accept /^\s*-\s+/ while a list key is open, or say in the error that '- item' lines must be indented under their key. Update the doc comment in both copies.

title: A trailing '# comment' on a match line becomes part of the regex, so the lens never fires
detail: Only whole-line '# comment' lines are skipped. 'match: foo # catch foo' parses without error, and the regex becomes 'foo # catch foo', which needs that literal text. The lens loads, is counted in 'loaded' and never fires, and nothing reports it. An author used to YAML inline comments gets a check that is silently off. Verified with parseLens. The same code is in src/lib/kit/lenses.js.
fix_hint: State in the header comment that inline comments are not supported and that the value is taken verbatim, or refuse a scalar that contains ' #' with a file:line error (other than on match, where '#' may be meant literally, warn instead).

title: Filter drivers and core.attributesFile in config.worktree are never discovered, so their clean filter runs
detail: Driver discovery reads only `git config --local` (.git/config plus includes). With extensions.worktreeConfig=true, git also reads $GIT_DIR/config.worktree, and `--local` does not see it. Traced on git 2.43: in an untrusted repo, `git config --worktree filter.evil.clean "sh -c 'touch PWN; cat'"` plus `git config --worktree core.attributesFile .git/evilattrs`, where .git/evilattrs is `* filter=evil` (inside .git, which the .gitattributes walk skips). Then modify a tracked file and run `node cli.js safe-git --dir r1 -- diff` (or `status`). The name `evil` is not in the override list, and the clean filter runs and creates PWN. The same gap applies to a linked worktree, whose config.worktree lives in .git/worktrees/<x>/. In that case the code also reads gitDir/info/attributes, not commonDir/info/attributes.
fix_hint: Read every config git will use, apart from system and global: use `git config --includes -z --get-regexp` without --local under the hardened env, which excludes system and global, or add `--worktree`. Look up core.attributesFile the same way. Read info/attributes from the common dir. Add a test with a filter set in config.worktree.

title: Abbreviated long options bypass the deny-list (cat-file --textc runs textconv)
detail: checkReadArgs matches the denied options exactly. git's parse-options accepts any unambiguous prefix, and cat-file adds no --no-textconv because it is not in DIFFING. Traced: in a repo with `diff.tc.textconv = sh -c 'touch PWN2; ...'` set in its local config and `* diff=tc` in .gitattributes, `node cli.js safe-git --dir r2 -- cat-file --textc HEAD:f.txt` exits 0 and creates PWN2, which means the repo's own command ran. The exact `--textconv` form is refused, as the test at line 92 checks, but the abbreviated form is not.
fix_hint: Refuse any option that is a prefix of a denied long option (for each long option, check `name.startsWith(arg.split('=')[0].slice(2))` with a length of at least 3). Also override `diff.<name>.textconv=` for every `diff=` driver named in the attributes, as already done for filters. Add tests for `cat-file --textc` and `--textconv` abbreviations.

title: Repo config format.pretty + gpg.program runs a program on a plain `log`/`show`
detail: STATIC_OVERRIDES switch off log.showSignature, and checkReadArgs refuses %G in argv, but neither gpg.program/gpg.ssh.program/gpg.x509.program nor format.pretty / pretty.<alias> is overridden. A hostile repo with `format.pretty=%H %G?`, `gpg.program=<script>` and a commit that has a gpgsig header makes `safeGit(dir, ['log','-1'])` or `['show','-s','HEAD']` run the script. I reproduced this on git 2.43 with a marker file. The same happens via `log --format=<alias>` with pretty.<alias>=%G?, and via `for-each-ref --format=%(signature)`, which the %G regex does not catch.
fix_hint: Add `-c gpg.program=false -c gpg.ssh.program=false -c gpg.x509.program=false -c format.pretty=medium` to STATIC_OVERRIDES (and refuse %(signature) in argv, or rely on the gpg overrides); add a regression test with a signed-looking commit.

title: Submodule work trees run their own clean filters during status/diff/describe --dirty
detail: Driver discovery reads only the outer repo's config and skips every `.git` dir, but status, diff, diff-files, diff-index and describe --dirty start a child git inside a checked-out submodule, which reads that submodule's .git/config and .git/info/attributes. Repro: outer repo with gitlink `sub`, `sub/.git/config` filter.zz.clean=<script>, `sub/.git/info/attributes` `* filter=zz`, and sub/f rewritten with the same size and a new mtime. Each of `status --porcelain`, `diff`, `diff-files`, `diff-index HEAD` and `describe --always --dirty` through safeGit then created the marker. The propagated -c covers hooks and fsmonitor, but not driver names that appear only in the submodule.
fix_hint: Pass `--ignore-submodules=all` (status/diff family) and `-c diff.ignoreSubmodules=all`, or refuse when the tree has gitlinks with a populated .git. Also scan nested .git/config and info/attributes, or refuse on nested .git dirs.

title: protocol.allow=never is overridden by repo protocol.<name>.allow; GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH is the only guard
detail: protocol.<name>.allow takes precedence over protocol.allow, so a repo that sets `extensions.partialClone=origin`, `remote.origin.promisor=true`, `remote.origin.url=ext::sh -c touch% M` and `protocol.ext.allow=always` gets a command run on any lookup of a missing object (for example `cat-file -t <unknown sha>`). With the wrapper's env minus GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH, git 2.43 created the marker. GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH only exists in git builds that include the 2024 CVE fix (2.45.1 and the backports), so on older git the transport override does not hold.
fix_hint: Also override protocol.<name>.allow=never for ext/file/ssh/http(s)/git and for every protocol.*.allow key found in the repo config, and set remote.<n>.promisor=false / remote.<n>.url= for each remote, or refuse when extensions.partialClone is set.

title: Override cache fingerprint ignores included config files
detail: fingerprint() stats only config, config.worktree and info/attributes of the git and common dirs. A filter driver or core.attributesFile added through an include.path / includeIf file (for example a work-tree file) after the first call reuses the stale overrides for the rest of the process, so the new driver is not switched off. The header comment says overrides are 'keyed by the stat of its config' and names only .gitattributes as needing fresh:true.
fix_hint: Fingerprint every file from `git config --list --show-origin --includes`, or skip the cache when the config uses include.*/includeIf.*; document it.

title: Shadow copy has no size cap: a sparse packed-refs/index/shallow/sharedindex fills /tmp
detail: buildShadow copies packed-refs, shallow, ORIG_HEAD.., index and every sharedindex.* with fs.copyFile and no size limit (only lstat isFile is checked). A file made with `truncate -s` takes no disk in the untrusted repo (e.g. unpacked from a tarball) but is written out in full to os.tmpdir(). Traced: r6/.git/index = `truncate -s 2G` (4 KB on disk); `node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js safe-git --dir r6 -- rev-parse HEAD` wrote 2049 MB into /tmp/safe-git-shadow-*/ before answering (exit 0). With packed-refs at 3G sparse: 3073 MB written, 11.6 s, while plain `git rev-parse HEAD` just reads it and fails in 2.6 s without writing. A `truncate -s 1T` file fills the shared /tmp/root disk (ENOSPC for every other process) on every call, including plain rev-parse HEAD.
fix_hint: Cap each copied file (packed-refs/shallow/pseudo refs by a sane limit, index/sharedindex by e.g. a few hundred MB or by comparing st.blocks*512 to st.size) and refuse (KitExit 2) above it; copy with a bounded stream that stops at the cap instead of copyFile.

title: refs/ symlinked to an outside folder is copied eagerly and recursively
detail: copyTree skips symlinks only BELOW the top: fs.readdir(commonDir/refs) follows a refs symlink (and looksLikeGitDir's stat accepts it), so the whole target tree is copied into the shadow on every call. Traced: r1/.git/refs -> outside/ made a file outside the repo appear as refs/heads/SECRET_from_outside in safe-git for-each-ref and copied a 200 MB file for rev-parse HEAD; r2/.git/refs -> /usr made `safe-git rev-parse HEAD` run 132 s and copy >2.5 GB of /usr into /tmp (plain git answers in 2 ms because it never walks refs/ for that). Same for a linked worktree's gitDir/refs (line 457). refs -> / or $HOME reads every readable file of the user into /tmp and can exhaust disk.
fix_hint: lstat commonDir/refs (and gitDir/refs) and refuse or skip it when it is not a real directory; also bound the total bytes/entries copyTree will copy.

title: Every call refuses on an ordinary JS checkout: .gitattributes walk counts ignored node_modules
detail: attributeFiles walks the whole work tree (ignored folders included, only '.git' skipped) and throws KitExit 2 past MAX_DIRS=20000, before any git command runs. Traced: repo with node_modules in .gitignore and 21211 folders under it -> `safeGit(r3, ['rev-parse','HEAD'])` fails 'more than 20000 folders ... cannot all be checked'. Installed node_modules / vendor / build trees routinely exceed 20000 folders, so even rev-parse HEAD is refused there, and the walk also re-runs (seconds of I/O) on every call.
fix_hint: Do not walk ignored or untracked folders: take attribute file paths from the index (`ls-files -z -- '*.gitattributes' .gitattributes` via the shadow) plus info/attributes, or skip folders git would not read attributes from; keep a cap only for tracked folders.

title: core.fsmonitor=false runs a program named 'false' on git 2.16-2.35
detail: Before git 2.36 core.fsmonitor is a hook PATH, not a boolean: git_config_get_fsmonitor only treats an EMPTY value as off, so `-c core.fsmonitor=false` makes status/diff run `sh -c 'false ...'` as the fsmonitor hook on every call (PATH-resolved, run from the work tree). Results stay correct (hook fails, full scan), but the wrapper itself spawns a program on older git, contrary to its no-program claim.
fix_hint: Use `core.fsmonitor=` (empty): off on old git, and parsed as false by git >= 2.36's maybe-bool.

title: 'no system or global config' is untrue on git < 2.32
detail: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL was added in git 2.32; older git ignores it and reads ~/.gitconfig and $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config in every shadow run, while the header (line 28) states no global config is read. The user's own config is trusted so no exploit is traced, but the stated isolation and the tests' assumptions do not hold on older git.
fix_hint: Also point HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME at the empty scratch folder for the git runs, or state the git >= 2.32 requirement in the header.

title: git is spawned by bare name with cwd set to the untrusted repo, so a git binary inside the repo can run
detail: defaultGitRunner calls spawnSync('git', ...) and passes no absolute path, and every shadow run (raw() in prepare) uses cwd: info.loc.real, which is the untrusted folder. On Windows, libuv's search_path checks the child's cwd before PATH, so a git.exe committed at the repo root runs on every safe-git call. On POSIX the same happens when PATH has an empty or relative entry. I reproduced it on Linux: repo r1 with an executable ./git (`touch PWN_PATH; exec /usr/bin/git "$@"`), then `PATH=":$PATH" node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js safe-git --dir r1 -- rev-parse HEAD` created PWN_PATH and still printed the right SHA. `PATH=":$PATH" git -C r1 rev-parse HEAD`, run from /, did not. A git clone keeps the executable bit, so bbs/fetch.js headOf(dest) goes through the same path on a fresh foreign clone. This is the one program-run guard the wrapper does not have.
fix_hint: Resolve git to an absolute path once, from PATH entries that are absolute (skip empty, '.' and relative entries) and not inside the repo, and spawn that path. Alternatively run every git child with cwd = the private scratch folder and pass the repo location only through GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/-C. Add a test with an executable ./git and PATH=":$PATH".

title: Index copied verbatim: an entry named ../x makes diff/status read and print files outside the repo
detail: The index is copied byte for byte into the shadow. Git does not run verify_path on index entries when it reads the index from disk, so an entry whose name starts with ../ makes diff-files, diff and status lstat and read GIT_WORK_TREE/../<path>. Traced: in repo r2, I renamed the index entry `zzzzzzzzzz/sec` to `../outside/sec` (same length, SHA-1 trailer recomputed). `node cli.js safe-git --dir r2 -- diff` then exited 0 and printed `+TOP SECRET KEY`, the contents of outside/sec, a file outside the repository. `status --porcelain` listed `AM ../outside/sec`. A symlink-leading path is blocked by git, but `..` is not. bbs/fetch.js clones into a predictable folder below the user's project, so an attacker can choose a depth such as `../../../../../.env` that reaches the user's project secrets. The page header states that reads stay inside the repo and shadow.
fix_hint: After building the shadow, run `ls-files -z --cached` (or `--stage`) on it before any work-tree command. Refuse with KitExit 2 when any entry is absolute or has an empty, '.', '..' or '.git' component (a case-insensitive check for '.git'). Add a regression test that patches an index entry to ../outside.

title: Untrusted include.path is followed to any path (outside the repo, FIFOs, UNC shares) though git never uses that config
detail: inspect() reads the repo config with `git config --file <f> --includes`. Git therefore opens every include.path the hostile repo names, at any absolute path, even though the shadow never uses those values: only driver names are taken, and no driver can be defined because git never reads the repo config. Traced with a FIFO: `include.path=<outside>/fifo` and a writer blocked on the FIFO. The writer was released (marker OPENED created), which shows safe-git opened a path outside the repo. With no writer, `safe-git --dir r5 -- rev-parse HEAD` hangs for the full 60 s INTERNAL_TIMEOUT on every call and then fails with `cannot run git: spawnSync git ETIMEDOUT`. On Windows the same key set to a `//attacker-host/share/x` UNC path makes the wrapper open an SMB connection with the user's NTLM credentials, which is egress to a host the attacker picks. Plain git would also do this, but reading the config through the shadow exists to avoid touching repo config at all.
fix_hint: Read the config files with --no-includes. Included files can only add driver names, and the shadow never defines drivers, so nothing is lost. Alternatively, refuse when include.*/includeIf.* is present. Add a test with include.path pointing at a FIFO and check that it neither opens nor waits.

title: Kit-missing fallback still spawns bare 'git' with cwd inside the fresh clone, so a git committed to the repo runs
detail: bbs and kit are separate plugins (src/plugins/bbs.js and src/plugins/kit.js install helpers/bbs and helpers/kit independently), so bbs without kit is a supported install, and loadSafeGit() then returns null. headOf then calls runGit -> execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse','HEAD'], { cwd: dest }). The name 'git' is looked up through an empty or '.' PATH entry on POSIX, and in the cwd first on Windows (libuv search_path). cloneEnv keeps PATH as it is. I proved it with a repo whose root holds a committed 0755 file named 'git' that touches a marker and then execs /usr/bin/git. headOf(repo, {PATH:':/usr/bin:/bin'}, { load: async () => null }) created markers/repo-git-ran. The same call through the kit path (default load) created no marker. This is the hole round 4 fixed in safe-git (resolveGit), left open on the one path that touches a just-cloned foreign checkout.
fix_hint: In runGit, spawn git by an absolute path found only in the absolute PATH entries (reuse the resolveGit logic, or copy it into bbs so it works without the kit), and/or run the fallback rev-parse with cwd outside dest using --git-dir=<dest>/.git.

title: A subfolder --dir silently re-roots pathspecs to the top; usage text never says so
detail: Every command runs as if from the top of the work tree. Only the module header comment says this; the usage string a CLI user sees does not. With repo r holding sub/f, `safe-git --dir r/sub -- log --oneline -- f` returns {stdout:'', code:0}: an empty history with a success code for a file that has history. In git, `cd r/sub && git log -- f` shows the commit. `ls-files` from r/sub prints 'sub/f' (top-relative), and `show HEAD:./f` fails with git's own 'relative path syntax can't be used outside working tree', which says nothing about safe-git. Someone pointing --dir at a subfolder gets a wrong, silent answer and nothing tells them why.
fix_hint: State in `usage` that paths are relative to the repository top whatever --dir names. Also report the prefix: add a `prefix` field to the result, or a stderr note when loc.real is below top and the argv has pathspecs. Alternatively, refuse a relative pathspec after '--' when --dir is a subfolder.

title: Forgetting '--' reports 'unknown flag log'; refusals say 'refused' twice
detail: `safe-git --dir r log` fails with 'kit: unknown flag log (usage: ...)'. 'log' is not a flag; the real mistake is the missing '--' before the git arguments. `safe-git --help` gives the same 'unknown flag' message. Policy refusals print 'kit: refused: git option --ext would re-enable ...; refused' and 'kit: refused: git rev-parse --git-dir ...; refused': cli.js already adds the 'refused:' prefix (lines 723, 726, 788).
fix_hint: When the argument does not start with '-', say 'git arguments must follow "--" (usage: ...)'. Handle --help/-h by printing the usage. Drop the trailing '; refused' from the KitExit 2 messages.

title: CLI exits 0 when the git command fails
detail: `safe-git --dir r -- log nosuchref` prints {code:128, stderr:'fatal: ambiguous argument ...'} but the process exits 0. cli.js documents '0 ok' and honours result.exit, which safe-git's run never sets. A shell caller using `kit safe-git ... && next` or `set -e` treats a failed git read as success. The usage does say that { code } is printed, so this is drift, not hidden behaviour.
fix_hint: In run(), return { ...result, exit: result.code === 0 ? 0 : 1 } (the code is still in the JSON), or document in the usage that the exit status is 0 whenever git ran.

title: '--no-index is refused' is untrue: diff of two outside paths runs no-index implicitly
detail: The header and DENIED_LONG say --no-index is refused. git diff switches to no-index on its own when both paths are outside the work tree. `safe-git --dir r -- diff /abs/o1 /abs/o2` returned a diff of the two files outside the repo with code 1. No program runs, because --no-ext-diff and --no-textconv are still inserted. The documented deny list still misstates what the wrapper allows.
fix_hint: For diff, refuse when the two non-option arguments are paths outside the work tree (or any absolute path argument), or correct the header to say the implicit no-index form is allowed.

title: Driver discovery opens any path the repo's core.attributesFile names, and follows symlinked attribute files, though git in the shadow never reads them
detail: overridesFor takes core.attributesfile from the untrusted repo config and calls readCapped(path.resolve(base, value)). readCapped uses fs.stat and readFile, so it follows symlinks and accepts any absolute path. It does the same for gitDir/info/attributes, even when info/ is a symlink (buildShadow skips a symlinked info/ but this read does not), and for every work-tree .gitattributes, which git >= 2.32 does not follow when it is a symlink. Traced on git 2.43: repo h with `core.attributesFile=<scratch>/outside/attrs` (a file outside the repo holding `* filter=fromoutside`). `strace` of `cli.js safe-git --dir h -- rev-parse HEAD` shows statx and openat of outside/attrs, and safeGitConfig(h) returns filter.fromoutside.* overrides, so the wrapper read a file outside the repository that the attacker chose. On Windows a value like `//attacker/share/x` makes the wrapper open an SMB connection with the user's NTLM credentials. Round 4 removed include.path reading for exactly this reason ('a UNC share that sends the user's credentials'). The shadow never sets core.attributesFile, and git does not follow symlinked .gitattributes, so none of these reads is needed for safety.
fix_hint: Drop core.attributesFile discovery, since the shadow config never sets it. Otherwise only accept a value that resolves inside commonDir/gitDir/top, refused when absolute or UNC. Read every attribute file with lstat + O_NOFOLLOW, as copyCapped does, and skip symlinks. Add a test with core.attributesFile pointing at an outside file and assert it is never opened.

title: 'Nothing is cached' / 'there is no cache any more' is untrue: the git path is cached per PATH for the process lifetime
detail: The header says nothing is cached, and the comment on clearSafeGitCache (line 470) says there is no cache. resolveGit keeps gitPathCache, keyed by the PATH string, and clearSafeGitCache does not clear it. In a long-running process, if the git it found is removed or moved (an upgrade that relocates /usr/local/bin/git), every later call fails with 'cannot run git: spawnSync ... ENOENT' even though PATH has another git, and clearSafeGitCache() does not help. The test at test/kit-hardened-git-read-on-untrusted-repo.test.js:460 is still named 'invalidates the cache' although there is no config cache to invalidate.
fix_hint: Make clearSafeGitCache clear gitPathCache, or drop the cache. Change the header to 'repository state is never cached'. Rename the test to '... is seen by the next call'.

title: Implicit no-index happens when EITHER path is outside the work tree, not 'both'
detail: The header (line 73) and the comment at line 764 say git diff goes no-index on its own 'when both paths lie outside the work tree'. git's condition is that at least one path is outside. Traced on git 2.43: in repo r, `git diff a.txt <abs>/out.txt` printed the diff of a.txt against the outside file, with '+secret'. The code is safe because it refuses each escaping argument. But the stated rule invites someone to relax the check to 'refuse only when both are outside', which would reopen the outside-file read.
fix_hint: Say 'when either path lies outside the work tree' in both places.

title: Exact, harmless options (diff --text, rev-list --filter=...) are refused with a message claiming they re-enable code execution
detail: The prefix rule refuses any long option that is a prefix of a denied option, including real options that git matches exactly before it tries abbreviations. `safe-git --dir h -- diff --text` exits 2 with 'git option --text would re-enable code execution, write a file or read a submodule', but --text is -a (treat as text), not --textconv. `rev-list --filter=blob:none --objects HEAD` is refused the same way, but rev-list's --filter is an object filter, not cat-file's --filters. The refusal text states something false about these options. The test at line 508 claims ordinary long options keep working, and it does not cover them.
fix_hint: Exempt exact option names that the subcommand really has (at least 'text' for the diffing commands and 'filter' for rev-list/log) from the prefix rule, or word the message as 'is, or abbreviates, a denied option'.

title: 'then behaviour is unchanged' / 'existing behaviour' are untrue: the kit-missing path now runs a different command
detail: loadSafeGit's comment says that when the kit is missing 'behaviour is unchanged'. The test at test/kit-hardened-git-read-on-untrusted-repo.test.js:349 is named 'keeps the plain call (existing behaviour)'. Both are wrong after round 5: the fallback now runs `git --git-dir <dest>/.git rev-parse HEAD` from the clone's parent folder, with git resolved to an absolute path, and the test asserts exactly that new argv. A reader auditing the bbs-without-kit install is told nothing changed there.
fix_hint: Reword to 'falls back to the plain runner (absolute git, --git-dir, cwd outside the clone)' and rename the test accordingly.

title: A symlinked work-tree .gitattributes is skipped 'as git does', but git then reads the index blob, so drivers named there are not listed
detail: workTreeAttributes skips a .gitattributes that lstat finds (readAttributesFile returns '' for a symlink) and `continue`s, without falling back to the index. git 2.43 in the CHECKIN direction fails open_nofollow with ELOOP, then reads the same path from the index (attr.c read_attr: read_attr_from_file, then read_attr_from_index). Traced: repo with `* diff=evil` committed as a regular .gitattributes, work-tree copy replaced by `ln -s /dev/null .gitattributes`. Plain `git check-attr diff a.txt` prints `a.txt: diff: evil`, and `git -c diff.evil.textconv=... diff` runs the textconv. safeGitConfig(repo) lists no diff.evil.* / filter.evil.* overrides. Nothing runs through safeGit today, because the shadow config defines no driver. But the header promises an override for every driver in 'a work-tree .gitattributes that git would read', and the inline comment 'a symlink: skipped, as git does' misstates git's behaviour. The previous readCapped had the same gap.
fix_hint: When lstat shows a non-regular file (symlink), take the index branch (`cat-file -s` / `cat-file blob :rel`) rather than skipping. Fix the comment, and add a test with a regular .gitattributes in the index and a symlink in the work tree.

title: The caller's git command runs with no timeout when none is passed (CLI always), so a FIFO .gitattributes hangs safe-git forever
detail: makeCtx sets ctx.timeout = timeout ?? INTERNAL_TIMEOUT, but safeGit calls exec(argv, { input, timeout }) and raw() builds { ..., timeout: ctx.timeout, ...extra }. The explicit `timeout: undefined` in extra overwrites the default, so the user's command (and describeDirty's three calls) run with spawnSync timeout undefined. The CLI never passes a timeout. I traced it on git 2.43 with a repo that has a commit, a modified a.txt, and `mkfifo .gitattributes` in the work tree. `cli.js safe-git --dir <repo> -- diff HEAD` blocks forever (killed by `timeout 20`, exit 124). A spy runner shows the four internal calls finish with timeout=60000 and the final `diff ... HEAD` gets timeout=undefined. git opens the FIFO with O_RDONLY to look up the diff driver and waits for a writer. With { timeout: 3000 } the same call ends with KitExit 1 (ETIMEDOUT). safe-git itself avoids FIFOs (O_NONBLOCK reads, --no-includes 'a FIFO that hangs the read'), but the git it starts does not, and a repo unpacked from an archive can carry a FIFO. The bbs caller passes timeoutMs, so it is not affected.
fix_hint: Fill in the default before spreading: in safeGit/describeDirty pass `timeout: ctx.timeout` (or in raw use `timeout: extra.timeout ?? ctx.timeout`). Add a test with a FIFO .gitattributes and an injected short default, checking that the CLI path returns a timeout error.

title: CLI drops piped stdin: `--stdin` / `--batch*` commands return empty output with exit 0
detail: cli.js hands every verb io.stdin and io.stdinIsTTY, but safe-git's run() never reads them and calls safeGit without `input`, so git's stdin is closed. I traced `echo HEAD | cli.js safe-git --dir r -- cat-file --batch-check` and `echo HEAD | cli.js safe-git --dir r -- rev-list --stdin` against a repo with one commit. Both print {stdout:'', code:0, exit:0}, which reads as 'no such object' or 'no commits' instead of an error. The library API supports `input`, the allow-list admits these stdin-reading options (cat-file --batch/--batch-check/--batch-command, rev-list/log/diff-tree --stdin, name-rev --annotate-stdin), and the usage text never says the CLI cannot take stdin.
fix_hint: In run(), when !io.stdinIsTTY and the git args use a stdin-reading option, pass `input: await io.stdin()` to safeGit. Read stdin only in that case, so an open pipe does not block other commands. Otherwise refuse those options in the CLI with a message (KitExit 1). Add a CLI test that pipes HEAD into cat-file --batch-check.

title: A `limits` key set to undefined replaces the default: entries cap silently off, file caps crash with RangeError
detail: makeCtx and buildShadow merge with { ...DEFAULT_LIMITS, ...limits }, so a caller passing { limits: { index: opts.maxIndex } } with maxIndex unset overrides the default with undefined. Traced: safeGit(repo, ['rev-parse','HEAD'], { limits: { index: undefined } }) and { total: undefined } both throw a raw RangeError ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE (Buffer.alloc(NaN) in copyCapped) instead of a KitExit. { entries: undefined } turns off the refs/ walk cap entirely (`++entries > undefined` is never true). Neither happens through the CLI or the bbs caller, which pass no limits.
fix_hint: Merge only defined, finite, non-negative numbers (e.g. filter Object.entries(limits) by Number.isFinite(v) && v >= 0), or throw KitExit 1 for an invalid limit.

title: The stdin guard misses name-rev --annotate-stdin and show-ref --exclude-existing, so both still return empty output with exit 0
detail: The round-8 fix refuses a command without --input - only when an argument is exactly --stdin or starts with --batch. Two allow-listed commands read stdin under other option names: `name-rev --annotate-stdin` (and git's accepted abbreviation `--annotate`) and `show-ref --exclude-existing[=pattern]`. Traced on git 2.43 with a repo that has branch feat: `echo <HEAD sha> | git name-rev --annotate-stdin` prints '<sha> (feat)', and `printf 'refs/heads/feat\nrefs/heads/nope\n' | git show-ref --exclude-existing` prints 'refs/heads/nope'. Through `cli.js safe-git --dir r -- name-rev --annotate-stdin` and `... -- show-ref --exclude-existing`, both print {stdout:'', code:0, exit:0}. This is the same silent wrong answer round 8 reported for --stdin and --batch: 'no names' or 'every ref exists'.
fix_hint: Match the stdin readers per subcommand and include prefixes: name-rev with a prefix of annotate-stdin (at least 'annotate') or stdin, show-ref with --exclude-existing[=...], plus the existing --stdin and --batch* forms. Add a CLI test for each.

title: cat-file --batch-all-objects needs no stdin, but can't be run from a terminal
detail: `/^--batch/` also matches --batch-all-objects, which lists the object store and reads no stdin. From an interactive shell, `safe-git --dir r -- cat-file --batch-check --batch-all-objects` is refused with 'reads stdin: pass --input -'. Adding `--input -` is then refused with '--input - needs piped stdin, not a terminal' (traced with script(1)). The command only works with `--input - </dev/null`, which neither message suggests.
fix_hint: Exempt --batch-all-objects from the stdin rule. For example, require --input only for --batch* when --batch-all-objects is absent.

title: timeout is not validated: 0 silently turns off the hang guard, and other bad values throw a raw RangeError
detail: Round 8 validated `limits` (mergeLimits), but `timeout` still goes straight to spawnSync through `timeout ?? INTERNAL_TIMEOUT`. Traced with safeGit(r, ['rev-parse','HEAD'], { timeout }): with 0 the call succeeds with no time limit, so the FIFO .gitattributes hang fixed in round 8 comes back. With -1, '5000', Infinity, NaN or 1.5, it throws RangeError ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE instead of a KitExit. bbs headOf forwards cloneRepo's timeoutMs unchanged.
fix_hint: Validate timeout in makeCtx the same way as limits: undefined keeps INTERNAL_TIMEOUT; anything else must be a positive safe integer, or KitExit 1.

title: The 60 s cap on the user's command is undocumented and reported as 'cannot run git ... ETIMEDOUT' (exit 1)
detail: Since 2a0a9e8, every git child, including the user's own command, is killed after INTERNAL_TIMEOUT (60 s), and the CLI cannot raise it. Neither the header nor the usage mentions the cap. When it fires, the CLI prints 'kit: cannot run git: spawnSync /usr/bin/git ETIMEDOUT' and exits 1, which the usage defines as 'bad input'. Traced with a FIFO .gitattributes: exit 1 after 60.1 s. A legitimately slow read such as `log -S<string>` on a long history hits the same message. An output over the 256 MiB maxBuffer gives the equally opaque '... ENOBUFS'.
fix_hint: Map ETIMEDOUT and ENOBUFS to clear messages ('git took longer than 60 s, killed' / 'git output over 256 MiB'), and state both caps in the header and usage. Optionally add a --timeout CLI flag.

title: buildShadow's doc comment now sits above mergeLimits
detail: mergeLimits was inserted between buildShadow's JSDoc ('Build the shadow git dir inside scratch ...') and the function. Two doc blocks are now stacked on mergeLimits, and buildShadow, an export, has none.
fix_hint: Move the 'Build the shadow git dir' comment down to just above `export async function buildShadow`.

title: The repo's objects/info/alternates is followed to any path: git opens files outside the repo (FIFOs, UNC shares) and serves other repositories' objects
detail: GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY points at the untrusted repo's real objects/, so git reads its objects/info/alternates and follows every entry it lists, plus each alternate's own info/alternates, recursively. That is the same 'repo names any path' exposure the header says safe-git closed for include.path ('a FIFO or a UNC share it names is never touched'). Traced on git 2.43: (1) victim/.git/objects/info/alternates = /abs/outside/objects, whose info/alternates is a FIFO with a writer that touches a marker once the FIFO is opened. `safe-git --dir victim -- log --oneline` opened it and MARKER_opened_outside was created. (2) evil/.git/objects/info/alternates = /abs/secret/.git/objects. `safe-git --dir evil -- cat-file -p <blob sha>` printed TOPSECRET_MARKER from a different repository on the user's disk. On Windows an entry such as \\attacker\share\objects makes git connect over SMB and send the user's NTLM credentials. On a degraded network the same entry, or an NFS path, stalls every call until the timeout. The same class reaches safe-git's own discovery code: a .git file's gitdir: and a commondir file are lstat'ed/realpath'ed wherever they point (line 277, line 292). A tarball or shared-folder copy of a repo carries objects/info/alternates; a clone does not.
fix_hint: Before running git, read <commonDir>/objects/info/alternates as data (lstat to check it is a regular file, then a bounded read) and refuse (KitExit 2) when it lists any entry that is absolute, a UNC or drive path, or resolves outside commonDir. Alternatively, run git against a shadow objects dir whose info/ has no alternates. Apply the same inside-the-repo or not-UNC check to the gitdir: and commondir targets. Add a test using the FIFO and marker shown here.

title: Two git spawns per missing .gitattributes, each reloading the index: a repo with deleted attribute files takes minutes, and --timeout does not bound it
detail: workTreeAttributes runs `cat-file -s :rel` and then `cat-file blob :rel` as separate git processes for each tracked .gitattributes that is absent from the work tree. Each process re-reads the whole index, so the total time grows faster than the number of files. --timeout and the default 60000 ms apply to each child, not to the call, so the header's promise that 'a hostile repo cannot hang a read' does not hold. Measured: 1500 .gitattributes outside a sparse-checkout cone made `safe-git -- rev-parse HEAD` take 10.9 s (plain git: 0.002 s). 6000 deleted .gitattributes took 58.7 s, even with `--timeout 5000`. A hostile on-disk repo with tens of thousands of deleted .gitattributes stalls each call for many minutes. On older machines and on Windows, where a process spawn costs 30-50 ms, ordinary sparse monorepo checkouts become very slow too.
fix_hint: Take the blob ids from the `ls-files --stage` output already in hand, or from one `ls-files -s` of the listed paths. Then read all of them in one `cat-file --batch` call fed through `input`, checking each size against MAX_ATTR_BYTES from the batch header. Alternatively, put a deadline on the whole call that covers every git child.

title: Timeout/overflow messages name the command as 'git -c' instead of the subcommand
detail: exec puts the -c overrides in front of the argv, so args[0] is always '-c'. A FIFO .gitattributes with `safe-git --timeout 2000 -- status` prints 'kit: git -c took longer than 2000 ms and was stopped'. The ENOBUFS message reads 'git -c wrote more than 256 MiB' in the same way. The user cannot tell which step timed out: the config read, the index listing, the attributes listing or their own command. The test at test/...test.js:1707 checks only the 'took longer than' part.
fix_hint: Name the first argument that is not a -c pair, i.e. the subcommand after the overrides (or pass a label from the caller), and assert it in the existing timeout test.

title: Alternates refusal is bypassed by a symlinked objects/ or objects/pack: safe-git serves another repository's objects
detail: Round 10 refused objects/info/alternates because it 'serves other repositories' objects', but the same effect needs no alternates file. GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY is <commonDir>/objects (line 684); finishLocate only checks isDir (it follows symlinks), and nothing checks objects/ or objects/pack. Traced on git 2.43 with the CLI. (1) evil1/.git/objects -> /abs/secret/.git/objects. `safe-git --dir evil1 --input - -- cat-file --batch-all-objects --batch </dev/null` printed TOPSECRET_MARKER, the blob of a different repository on disk. --batch-all-objects needs no SHA. (2) evil2/.git/objects/pack -> /abs/secret/.git/objects/pack, with the repo's own loose objects still in place: the same command printed TOPSECRET_MARKER. A tarball or shared-folder copy of a repo carries symlinks just as it carries the alternates file that round 10 refused. safe-git already refuses a symlinked refs/ for this reason (copyTree), but not a symlinked objects/. Related: a .git symlink, or a `gitdir: ../secret/.git` file, opens the other repository outright (both traced: TOPSECRET_MARKER printed). Linked worktrees legitimately use gitdir:, so that case at least deserves a documented caveat.
fix_hint: In checkNoAlternates or finishLocate, lstat <commonDir>/objects and objects/pack (and objects/info) and refuse (KitExit 2) when one is a symlink, or when realpath(objects) is not inside commonDir. Add tests for both symlink layouts that use a marker blob, and list the remaining gitdir:/.git-symlink exposure in the header.

title: The UTF-8 'fail closed' check on index-only .gitattributes can be steered so that a trailing driver is silently dropped
detail: Each invalid byte decodes to U+FFFD (3 bytes), so with k invalid bytes buf[nl+1+size] lands on original byte size-2k. A blob with a '\n' at that offset passes the check, and its last 2k bytes are cut off without any error. Traced: a committed .gitattributes of 7 bytes 0xff + '# x\n* filter=evil' (no trailing newline), then deleted from the work tree. `git check-attr filter a.txt` reports 'evil', but safeGitConfig's overrides contain no filter.evil.* entries. The control case with ASCII bytes in place of 0xff does list filter.ctl.*. With no config able to define the driver nothing runs, but the code comment's 'fail closed rather than parse a shifted stream' guarantee does not hold.
fix_hint: Have the runner return stdout as a Buffer for this call (encoding 'buffer'/latin1), or read blobs with `cat-file --batch` and parse them by byte length before decoding. Alternatively, refuse when the decoded text contains U+FFFD. Add the 0xff test.

title: Index-only .gitattributes lookup asks for stage 0 only; git reads stage 2 of an unmerged file
detail: For a .gitattributes that is missing from the work tree, the code queries `:rel`, which is stage 0. During a conflicted merge the index holds only stages 1/2/3, and git's read_blob_data_from_index falls back to stage 2 ('ours'). Traced: the .gitattributes conflicted (stage 2 '* filter=ours2', stage 3 '* filter=theirs3'), then removed from the work tree. `git check-attr filter a.txt` gives 'ours2', while safeGitConfig lists neither driver: batch-check answered 'missing' and the file was skipped. This is a defence-in-depth gap only, since no config can define the driver.
fix_hint: When `:rel` is missing, also query `:2:rel` (or take the blob ids and stages straight from the `ls-files --stage` output already produced by checkIndexPaths).

title: Round-9 fix incomplete: `cat-file --batch-all-objects --batch` is still refused without --input -
detail: readsStdin exempts 'batch' and 'batch-check' when --batch-all-objects is present, but it tests every STDIN_LONG entry with startsWith. 'batch-command'.startsWith('batch') is true, so a plain `--batch` still counts as reading stdin. git matches the exact option --batch first, and with --batch-all-objects it reads no stdin. Traced from a TTY: `safe-git --dir repo -- cat-file --batch-all-objects --batch` exits 1 with 'reads stdin: pass --input -', while plain git prints every object. The test at test/...test.js:1669 covers only --batch-check.
fix_hint: Treat an exact option name as itself before the prefix match: if STDIN_LONG includes name, judge only that entry, and use the prefix match only for abbreviations. Add `--batch-all-objects --batch` to the TTY test.

title: Plain --exclude=<pattern> is taken for an abbreviation of --exclude-existing, so the CLI refuses it with an untrue 'reads stdin' message
detail: readsStdin only treats an exact STDIN_LONG name as exact; any other name that is a prefix of one counts as that option. `exclude` is a prefix of `exclude-existing`, but --exclude is a real option of describe, ls-files, log, rev-list, name-rev and for-each-ref, and git matches the exact name first. Traced with git 2.43: `cli.js safe-git --dir r -- describe --exclude=nothing --tags`, `ls-files --exclude=*.o --others`, `log --all --exclude=refs/tags/*`, `rev-list --all --exclude=refs/tags/*` and `name-rev --exclude=x HEAD` all exit 1 with 'describe with these options reads stdin: pass --input - before `--`'. None of them reads stdin (plain git answers `v1-1-gb976efe`). The message sends the user after stdin, which is the wrong cause; the only way through is to pipe empty stdin with --input -.
fix_hint: Keep a per-subcommand exact-name set as EXACT_SAFE does (exclude is exact for every allowed subcommand except show-ref), or count a name only when it is not itself a real option of the subcommand. Add a CLI test for `describe --exclude=x` and `rev-list --all --exclude=x`.

title: Symlink check under objects/ stops one level down: a symlinked objects/info/commit-graphs/*.graph or commit-graph-chain is followed outside the repo
detail: checkObjectsNotLinked only walks objects/ and its direct subfolders, but git also reads objects/info/commit-graphs/graph-<hash>.graph and commit-graph-chain, which are two levels down. Traced: clone, `git commit-graph write --split --reachable`, replace the .graph file with a symlink to a FIFO outside the repo, then `cli.js safe-git --dir cg --timeout 3000 -- log --oneline -1`. git opens the outside file and blocks until the timeout ('git log took longer than 3000 ms ... raise it with --timeout'), so every read of that repo fails after the default 60 s. A symlink to a regular file or a network path is opened the same way. The header (line 26-27) says 'any symlink inside it' is refused, and the threat model says nothing outside the repo is read. This is the round-11 fix only partly done.
fix_hint: Walk objects/info/commit-graphs too (or recurse with a depth cap of 2 under info/), refuse a symlink there, and add a test with a symlinked split commit-graph file and chain.

title: A .gitattributes in a folder whose name is not UTF-8 is never read, so its drivers are not listed
detail: ls-files output is decoded as UTF-8, so a byte such as \xff in a folder name becomes U+FFFD. lstat of that rebuilt path fails, so the file is treated as gone from the work tree, and the cat-file lookup misses it too. Traced: a repo with `d\xff/.gitattributes` = `* filter=evil` and `ok/.gitattributes` = `* filter=good` gives overrides for `good` only. git itself reads both. No program runs, because the shadow config defines no drivers, but the header's claim that every driver in a work-tree .gitattributes git would read gets switched off does not hold.
fix_hint: Run that ls-files with binary: true and work with the raw path bytes (Buffer paths for lstat/open, raw bytes on cat-file stdin), or refuse when a listed path does not round-trip through UTF-8.

title: Header says another repository is reached only through a .git file or commondir, but a symlinked .git silently reads another repository
detail: Lines 26-30 refuse a symlinked objects/ or any symlink under it because it 'would read another repository's objects', and then name a .git file (gitdir:) or commondir as the one documented way to reach another repository. locateRepo (line 302) stats .git with fs.stat, which follows symlinks, and finishLocate realpaths it, so a .git that is a symlink to another repository is accepted with no refusal and no caveat. Traced on git 2.43: secret/ is a repo with a commit 'SECRETMSG'; evil/.git -> /abs/secret/.git; `node src/lib/kit/cli.js safe-git --dir evil -- log --oneline` exits 0 and prints '5999f31 SECRETMSG'. This is the same effect the objects/ symlink refusal exists to stop. A tarball or shared-folder copy can carry it as easily as the symlinked objects/ that round 11 reported, and round 11's detail already called out this exact case as needing a documented caveat. A reader of the header (and of the usage) is told that symlinks leading to other repositories are refused, and that the only exception is gitdir:/commondir.
fix_hint: Either refuse a .git that is a symlink (lstat it in locateRepo, as refs/ and objects/ are handled), or add it to the documented exception next to the gitdir:/commondir sentence, and add a test for whichever behaviour is chosen.

title: Header still says object alternates are honoured ('alternates there are object-only'), though they are now refused
detail: Line 12 says GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY points at the repo's real objects '(alternates there are object-only)', which says alternates are followed for objects. Since round 10, checkNoAlternates refuses any non-empty objects/info/alternates with KitExit 2, and lines 26-27 of the same header say so. The two sentences contradict each other.
fix_hint: Drop the parenthetical on line 12, or replace it with '(object alternates are refused, see below)'.

title: limits.entries now also caps the objects/ walk, but COPY LIMITS says it caps only entries under refs/
detail: checkObjectsNotLinked (line 651) counts every entry under objects/, including each loose object, against limits.entries and refuses past it with 'more than 100000 entries under .../objects; refusing to check them'. COPY LIMITS (line 36) documents the cap as '100000 entries walked under refs/', and the objects/ refusal does not say that the `limits` option raises it, though the copyCapped refusal does. So a repository with more than 100000 loose objects (gc.auto=0, or after a large unpack-objects) is refused for every command. Nothing in the header or the message explains why or how to proceed.
fix_hint: Say in COPY LIMITS that the entries cap covers refs/ and the objects/ symlink check, and mention the limits option (entries) in the objects/ refusal message.

title: Test asserts that rev-list --std reads stdin, but git rejects that abbreviation; the header still says 'any abbreviation'
detail: STDIN_OPTIONS['*'] counts any prefix of --stdin of at least 'std' for every subcommand, and the round-12 test asserts readsStdin(['rev-list','--std']) is true. rev-list, log and diff-tree parse --stdin with the revision parser, which takes no abbreviations. On git 2.43, `git rev-list --std` and `diff-tree --std` exit 129 with usage, and `git log --stdi` prints 'fatal: unrecognized argument: --stdi'. So the CLI refuses these with the untrue message '<cmd> with these options reads stdin: pass --input -'. Passing --input - then still fails in git. This is the same class of error round 12 fixed for --exclude, and the test now asserts it as intended behaviour. Separately, the header (lines 91-92) still says the CLI refuses 'STDIN_LONG, any abbreviation'. The code no longer uses STDIN_LONG and now applies per-subcommand minimum prefixes.
fix_hint: Count only the exact --stdin for the revision-parser commands (rev-list, log, show, diff-tree), and keep abbreviations for parse-options commands (name-rev, for-each-ref, cat-file, show-ref). Change the test to match, and reword lines 91-92 to describe STDIN_OPTIONS.

title: Work-tree .gitattributes texts are all held in memory with no total cap: sparse files take a few MB of disk and gigabytes of RAM, and crash node
detail: workTreeAttributes reads every listed .gitattributes in full (readAttributesFile, up to MAX_ATTR_BYTES = 4 MiB each) and keeps every decoded text in `out` until overridesFor has collected the driver names (line 700). Only the per-file size is capped. Nothing limits the file count or the total bytes, unlike the copy budget's `total`. The file system is the only thing read, so the header's own sparse-file threat (`truncate -s`) applies. Traced on git 2.43 / node 22: `git init r; git commit --allow-empty`, then 1100 folders d$i, each holding `truncate -s 4194303 d$i/.gitattributes`. These are untracked, so `ls-files --others` lists them. `du` says 4.5 MB. `safeGit(r, ['rev-parse','HEAD'])` peaks at 4.5 GiB RSS and takes 26 s. Under `--max-old-space-size=4096` (about the default heap on an 8 GB machine) it dies with 'FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit ... JavaScript heap out of memory'. The JS reads also run under no timeout, and 300 such files already take 14 s and 1.3 GiB. Cost grows linearly, so more files crash any heap size. Every command pays it, including a bare rev-parse HEAD.
fix_hint: Reduce each file to its driver-name Set as soon as it is read and drop the text (stream lines rather than concatenating). Put a total cap on the attribute bytes read per call, for example a limits.attributes defaulting to 64 MiB, and refuse with KitExit 2 past it, as copyCapped does with limits.total. Add a test with many sparse .gitattributes that asserts the refusal.

title: STDIN_OPTIONS comment says for-each-ref parses --stdin as a revision option; it is a parse-options boolean that git abbreviates
detail: for-each-ref has had --stdin since git 2.46, declared as OPT_BOOL(0, "stdin", ...) in builtin/for-each-ref.c. parse-options accepts unambiguous abbreviations, so `for-each-ref --std` reads its patterns from stdin. The '*' entry counts only the exact --stdin, and the comment names for-each-ref among the no-abbreviation commands. With git 2.46 or later, `safe-git -- for-each-ref --std` therefore runs with stdin closed instead of being asked for --input -. git reads no patterns and prints every ref, which is the 'empty input taken for a real answer' case the header (lines 93-95) says cannot happen.
fix_hint: Add 'for-each-ref': [['stdin', 'std']] to STDIN_OPTIONS, drop for-each-ref from the comment, and add for-each-ref --std to the reader test list.

title: Index-path check applies Windows rules on POSIX: a repository with a file named 'a:b', 'x/..\..\f' or 'x/C:\\t' is refused outright, so bbs cannot fetch it
detail: unsafeIndexPath treats a leading '<letter>:' as an absolute path and splits components on backslash on every platform. On Linux and macOS git treats these as ordinary file names: verify_path rejects backslashes only on Windows, and clone checks them out as literal names. Nothing is read outside the work tree. Reproduced on git 2.43: a repo with a top-level file 'a:b' gives `kit: refused: the index has an entry "a:b" (absolute path) that would make git read outside the work tree` (exit 2), even for `rev-parse HEAD`. With that file removed, 'tests/fixtures/..\..\evil.txt' (a typical path-traversal test fixture) is refused as component "..", and 'tests/fixtures/C:\\temp.txt' as component "". checkIndexPaths runs before every command with a work tree, so the whole repository becomes unreadable. Through the bbs caller, cloneRepo then fails ('git rev-parse HEAD failed after clone') and deletes the clone. The refusal message is also untrue on POSIX.
fix_hint: Split on '\\' and test /^[A-Za-z]:/ only when process.platform === 'win32', as git's verify_path does. Keep the '/'-based '', '.', '..' and .git-alias checks everywhere, and add POSIX 'good' cases ('a:b', 'x\\..\\y') to the unit test.

title: CLI crashes with a TypeError for a subcommand named like an Object.prototype key ('constructor', 'toString', '__proto__')
detail: readsStdin indexes STDIN_OPTIONS[args[0]] on the raw CLI argv before checkReadArgs runs. For 'constructor' it gets Object (a function) and spreads it, which throws. Reproduced: `cli.js safe-git --dir R -- constructor --x` prints `kit: (STDIN_OPTIONS[args[0]] || []) is not iterable` and exits 1, where every other unknown subcommand ('fetch --x') gets the documented exit-2 'not on the read-only allow-list' refusal.
fix_hint: Use `Object.hasOwn(STDIN_OPTIONS, args[0]) ? STDIN_OPTIONS[args[0]] : []`, or run checkReadArgs before readsStdin in run().

title: safeGitConfig JSDoc still says names from a .gitattributes listed by ls-files are included
detail: 656da9d stopped reading work-tree and index .gitattributes for driver names: overridesFor uses only config entries and info/attributes, and the tests now assert that such names are NOT listed. The exported function's doc still says overrides cover every driver named in 'info/attributes or a .gitattributes the shadow's ls-files lists'. A caller reading the API doc would expect a name used only in .gitattributes to appear in the result, and it does not.
fix_hint: Drop 'or a .gitattributes the shadow's ls-files lists'. Say that work-tree and index .gitattributes are not read, because the shadow config defines no driver.

title: Packaged test's 'runs nothing' check for a .gitattributes-only name has no driver behind it and no plain-git control
detail: The rewritten packaged block appends '*.txt filter=bad;name' to .gitattributes and then asserts that the markers folder is empty. No filter.bad;name driver is defined anywhere, and this line overrides the earlier 'filter=evil' for *.txt. So plain git would run nothing for f.txt either, and the assertion would pass even if the installed safe-git did read that name and somehow defined it.
