The unit tests use hiddenDriver plus a plain-git control for this, but the end-to-end packaged path (.claude/helpers copy through the installed CLI) has no proof that a name only in a .gitattributes never runs.
fix_hint: Define the driver through an include.path file (as hiddenDriver does) so that plain git runs it. Assert no marker through pkg.kit, then run plain git as the control and assert that the marker appears.

title: The repository's config file is read by two git spawns on every call
detail: inspect() calls readConfigFile(mainCfg) once for repoFormat and again in the `for (const f of files)` loop, because files starts with mainCfg. Counted with an injected runner: a plain `safeGit(dir, ['rev-parse','HEAD'])` spawns `git config --file .git/config --no-includes --list -z` twice before ls-files and the command. On a hostile repo this doubles the time a large config costs. A sparse 2 GiB .git/config takes about 20 s per read on git 2.43, so about 40 s per call, and each read gets its own full timeout. Two reads can also see different contents, with fmt taken from the first and core from the second.
fix_hint: Read the main config once, reuse its entries for repoFormat and as the first block of `entries`, and read only config.worktree in the loop.

title: checkIndexPaths doc says an output overflow is KitExit 1; it is exit 3 and the message tells the user to narrow a command they never ran
detail: defaultGitRunner turns ENOBUFS into KitExit(GIT_FAILED_EXIT = 3), 'git ls-files wrote more than 256 MiB of output; narrow the command'. When the internal `ls-files -z --stage` index listing overflows, the user, who asked for something like `rev-parse HEAD`, gets exit 3 ('git ran and failed' per the usage) and advice to narrow an ls-files they did not run. The doc comment claims 'KitExit 1, fail closed'. This can happen with a version-4 (prefix-compressed) index under the 256 MiB copy cap that expands to more than 256 MiB of listing.
fix_hint: In checkIndexPaths, catch the overflow and rethrow KitExit 1 (or 2) saying that the index listing is too large to check, or correct the comment.

title: Symlink check under objects/ fails open when a folder cannot be listed, so a symlinked loose object (or commit-graph/midx) in a write+exec-only folder is followed
detail: checkObjectsNotLinked does `try { entries = await fs.readdir(dir) } catch { return; }`, so any readdir error skips that whole subtree. git opens loose objects (objects/ab/<rest>), objects/info/commit-graph and objects/pack/multi-pack-index by NAME, which needs only search (x) permission on the folder. Traced as a non-root user (runuser -u nobody): repo evil/ with objects/d5 set to mode 0333 holding a symlink d5/52d1... -> /other/victim/.git/objects/d5/52d1...; `safeGit(evil, ['cat-file','-p','d552d1...'])` returns {stdout:'TOP SECRET', code:0}, reading another repository's object. As root (folder listable) the same repo is refused with KitExit 2 'is a symlink'. Modes like this survive tar/zip extraction of a hostile archive (333 & ~022 = 311 is still unlistable), so the documented guarantee 'any symlink inside objects/ is refused' and 'nothing outside the repo is opened' does not hold. A symlinked objects/info/commit-graph to a FIFO also blocks every call until the timeout.
fix_hint: Fail closed: in the walk, return only on ENOENT/ENOTDIR and throw refuse(`${dir} cannot be listed; safe-git cannot check it for symlinks`) for any other readdir error (EACCES, EPERM, EIO...). Add a test that chmods a loose-object folder to 0o333 and runs as a non-root user (skip when uid 0).

title: A git killed by a signal is reported as exit code 1, which describe --dirty and --quiet callers read as 'has differences'
detail: defaultGitRunner returns `code: r.status ?? 1`; spawnSync sets status null and signal (SIGSEGV, SIGABRT from git's BUG(), SIGKILL from the OOM killer) with no r.error, so a crash becomes code 1. describeDirty treats q.code === 1 as dirty: with a git whose diff-index dies of SIGSEGV, `safeGit(r, ['describe','--dirty','--tags'])` returns {stdout:'v1-dirty\n', code:0} (traced; a normal run prints 'v1'). Likewise `diff-index --quiet HEAD` / `diff --quiet` return code 1 with empty stderr, the documented 'differences found' answer, instead of a failure. A hostile repo crafted to crash git (corrupt index/pack hitting a git BUG/abort) turns that into a wrong 'dirty' result with exit 0.
fix_hint: When r.signal is set, throw KitExit(`git ${cmd} was killed by ${r.signal}`, GIT_FAILED_EXIT) (or return code 128 + signal number with a stderr note) so no caller can mistake a crash for exit 1; add a test with a stub git that kills itself.

title: A timeout while listing the index is reported as 'the index is too large' and as a policy refusal (exit 2)
detail: checkIndexPaths converts every KitExit with code GIT_FAILED_EXIT into refuse('the index is too large to check its paths ...'). defaultGitRunner uses that code for both ENOBUFS and ETIMEDOUT, so `--timeout 200` on a slow disk, or a loaded machine, prints 'kit: refused: the index is too large ... (git ls-files took longer than 200 ms ...)' and exits 2, while the header (line 91) says a timeout is exit 3. Callers that retry on 3 and treat 2 as a permanent policy verdict (bbs fails the fetch) get the wrong class.
fix_hint: Only map the output-overflow case to a refusal (distinguish it, e.g. by a `reason` field on the KitExit or by matching the ENOBUFS message) and let a timeout propagate as exit 3.

title: copyTree skips a refs/ folder it cannot list, so a loose ref in it silently resolves to a stale packed-refs value
detail: copyTree does `try { ents = await fs.readdir(s0, ...) } catch { return; }`. Round 16 made the objects/ walk fail closed on an unlistable folder, but the refs walk still fails open. Git opens loose refs by name, which a write+exec-only folder (0333/0311) allows. Reproduced as user nobody: a repo whose packed-refs has main=095aecf and whose loose refs/heads/main=3600c39, with refs/heads at mode 0333. Plain `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git log` give 3600c39 ('two'). safe-git gives 095aecf with code 0, and `log --oneline` shows only 'one'. That is a wrong answer with no error, not a refusal. An unreadable ref FILE gives an error (copyCapped rethrows EACCES), so only folders are affected. .claude/helpers/kit/safe-git.js is identical.
fix_hint: Handle readdir errors in copyTree as checkObjectsNotLinked does: return on ENOENT/ENOTDIR, otherwise refuse with KitExit 2 ('cannot list <dir>'). Add the 0333 refs/heads regression next to the round-16 one.

title: core.trustctime / core.checkStat are not carried into the shadow, so diff-files / diff-index report clean files as modified
detail: allowedCore copies only bare/ignorecase/precomposeunicode/quotepath/filemode/symlinks/autocrlf/eol. Users set core.trustctime=false or core.checkStat=minimal on file systems whose ctime or inode numbers change on their own: SMB/NFS/FUSE mounts, Windows backup or AV tools, VM shared folders, and indexes written by JGit. Without these keys, every stat-dirty entry counts as changed in the plumbing commands that do not refresh. Reproduced: repo with core.trustctime=false, then `chmod 600 a; chmod 644 a`. Plain `git diff-files --name-only` and `git diff-index --name-only HEAD` print nothing. safe-git prints 'a' for both (code 0). A script asking `diff-index --quiet HEAD` 'is it dirty?' gets the wrong answer. status and diff refresh in memory, so they are unaffected. These keys only change stat comparison and cannot name a program.
fix_hint: Add trustctime to CORE_BOOL and checkstat: ['default','minimal'] to CORE_ENUM, validated like the others. Add a test with core.trustctime=false and a ctime-only change.

title: Network-path refusal for gitdir:/commondir misses mixed-separator UNC paths (/\host\share) on Windows
detail: isNetworkPath only tests /^(\/\/|\\\\)/. On Windows, path.win32 treats '/' and '\\' alike, so a .git file holding `gitdir: /\evil\share\r` (or `\/evil/share/r`) passes the check. path.resolve then turns it into \\evil\share\r (checked: path.win32.resolve('C:\\work\\repo','/\\evil\\share\\r') === '\\\\evil\\share\\r'). looksLikeGitDir then lstats \\evil\share\r\HEAD, which opens an SMB connection to the attacker's host and sends the user's NTLM credentials. That happens before git runs and despite the header's 'network paths (//host, \\host) in a gitdir: file or commondir are refused'. Writing the .git file needs no symlink privilege, so an unpacked archive is enough. The same applies to commondir (line 325). The same check is also bypassed by a relative gitdir: naming a local symlink to a UNC target.
fix_hint: Test the RESOLVED path instead of the raw text: on win32, refuse when path.win32.resolve(base, value) starts with '\\\\' (this covers \\?\UNC\ too). Optionally readlink the target chain before stat/realpath. Add a test for '/\\host\\share' with platform injected.

title: limits.entries is checked only after readdir has loaded the whole folder, so one huge folder costs memory and time beyond the cap
detail: copyTree (line 778) and checkObjectsNotLinked (line 611) call fs.readdir, which builds a Dirent for every entry before the ++entries check runs. Measured: refs/heads/z with 1,000,000 empty files gives peak RSS 438 MB and 37.7 s before 'more than 100000 entries' is refused (the first 100k files are also copied one by one). Memory grows linearly, so about 10M entries (inodes only, no data) runs node out of heap despite the documented 100000-entry cap. None of this is bounded by --timeout.
fix_hint: Iterate with `for await (const e of await fs.opendir(dir))` so the cap stops the read early. Optionally count entries before copying any of them.

title: info/grafts is not copied, so history differs silently in repos that still use grafts, and the header does not list it
detail: Only info/exclude and info/attributes are copied from info/. Git (2.43 here) still honors $GIT_DIR/info/grafts, with a deprecation hint. Reproduced: with grafts 'c3 c1', plain `git log --oneline` shows c3, c1. safe-git shows c3, c2, c1 with code 0. The header's 'Not reproduced' list (line 98) covers reflogs, core.worktree, and so on, but not grafts. Older repos stitched together with grafts get a different history and no warning.
fix_hint: Copy info/grafts with copyCapped (it is data: commit ids only), or add grafts to the 'Not reproduced' list in the header.

title: A nested .git file (submodule or untracked folder) can still make git open a network path
detail: Network paths are refused only for the TOP-level .git gitdir: file and commondir (locateRepo/finishLocate, isNetworkPath line 628). git also reads the gitdir: file of every folder below the work tree that has a .git: (a) an untracked folder sub/.git, during status and ls-files -o (dir.c treat_directory -> is_nonbare_repository_dir -> read_gitfile_gently -> is_git_directory), and (b) a populated gitlink (submodule) folder mod/.git, during status, diff and diff-files, even with --ignore-submodules=all / diff.ignoreSubmodules=all. Reproduced with git 2.43 under strace: a repository with mod/.git (or sub/.git) containing 'gitdir: //evilhost/share/MARKER' makes safeGit(repo, ['diff-files']) / ['status','--porcelain'] / ['ls-files','-o'] spawn /usr/bin/git, which calls newfstatat("//evilhost/share/MARKER/HEAD"). On Linux that is a harmless local path, but on Windows it is a UNC path: git opens an SMB connection to evilhost and sends the user's NTLM credentials, the exact egress the header says is refused. An unpacked archive or copied repo (the case refuseNetworkLink is written for) can carry such files.
fix_hint: Before running a command that walks the work tree (status, diff*, ls-files -o, describe --dirty), refuse (KitExit 2) when any gitlink entry from the index check, or any folder found under the work tree, holds a .git file or symlink whose gitdir:/link text is a network path (isNetworkPath); at minimum check the folders of the 160000 entries already listed by checkIndexPaths, and walk untracked folders for .git files the same way.

title: Every input error repeats the full ~600-character usage string on one line
detail: run() adds the whole `usage` string to the unknown-flag, missing-`--`, no-command and reads-stdin errors (lines 1130, 1131, 1134, 1136). On stderr the specific complaint ('cat-file with these options reads stdin: pass --input - before `--`') then sits in front of one unbroken ~600-character parenthetical. A screen reader reads all of it, and a narrow terminal wraps it into a block where the actual error is hard to find (reproduced with `cli.js safe-git -- cat-file --batch`). The same text is also in .claude/helpers/kit/safe-git.js.
fix_hint: Keep the error to the specific complaint plus a short pointer such as '(see cli.js safe-git --help)', and leave the full usage to --help.

title: The reads-stdin refusal does not name the option that triggered it
detail: readsStdin() matches abbreviations (e.g. `name-rev --an`, `cat-file --batch-ch`, `show-ref --ex`), but the error only says '<subcommand> with these options reads stdin'. A user who typed an abbreviation, or has several options, cannot tell which argument to change without reading the STDIN_OPTIONS source.
fix_hint: Have readsStdin return the matching argument (or add a helper that does) and put it in the message, for example "`--an` (--annotate-stdin) reads stdin".

title: name-rev --s / --st (= --stdin) slip past the CLI stdin refusal and return an empty success
detail: STDIN_OPTIONS counts name-rev's --stdin only from the abbreviation 'std', but git's parse-options takes any unique prefix, and 'stdin' is the only name-rev option beginning with 's'. With git 2.43, `git name-rev --s` and `git name-rev --st` both run as --stdin (they print the deprecation warning). Reproduced: `cli.js safe-git --dir <repo> -- name-rev --st </dev/null` prints {stdout:'', code:0, exit:0}, while `--std` is refused. That contradicts the header (line 97), which says the CLI refuses stdin options 'with the abbreviations git accepts there, so an empty answer is never mistaken for a real one'. for-each-ref has the same problem at line 131: from git 2.46, before any other option starting with --st was added, --st uniquely means --stdin.
fix_hint: Make the shortest counted prefix 's' for name-rev's stdin and 'st' for for-each-ref's (no other option of those subcommands starts with them), and add `name-rev --s`/`--st` to the stdin-refusal test table.

title: rev-parse --is-bare-repository says true for a non-bare repo's .git dir
detail: shadowConfigText writes `bare = (top === null)` and ignores the repository's own core.bare. So when --dir names the .git of an ordinary repository (allowed by checkRepoRoot), `safe-git --dir repo/.git -- rev-parse --is-bare-repository` prints 'true'. Plain git run in that folder prints 'false' (reproduced). The header lists what the shadow does not reproduce, but this case is not on that list.
fix_hint: Answer --is-bare-repository the way revParsePosition answers its options (from core.bare/loc), or note this in the header's not-reproduced list.

title: Header allow-list of core keys omits trustctime and checkstat
detail: The header lists the core keys the shadow config carries (ignorecase, precomposeunicode, quotepath, filemode, symlinks, autocrlf, eol). The code (CORE_BOOL/CORE_ENUM, lines 411-413) also carries core.trustctime and core.checkstat, so the documented allow-list is not the real one.
fix_hint: Add trustctime and checkstat to the header list.

title: -O is labelled --open-files-in-pager, which is grep's meaning, not that of the allowed subcommands
detail: None of the allowed subcommands has --open-files-in-pager (it belongs to git grep, which is refused). For log, show and the diff family, -O<orderfile> reads an arbitrary file as the diff order file, and that is the real reason /^-O/ is refused. The header pairs the two, which misstates what is being blocked.
fix_hint: Describe it as `-O<orderfile> (reads any file)` and drop or separately justify open-files-in-pager.

title: Duplicate, stale JSDoc block on isNetworkPath
detail: Two consecutive /** */ comments describe isNetworkPath. The first (only //host or \\host) is stale: the code also matches mixed separators (/\\host, \\/host).
fix_hint: Delete the first comment line.

title: guarded-write with no piped stdin silently truncates the target to 0 bytes
detail: run() writes whatever io.stdin() returns. cli.js readStdin returns '' when stdin is a TTY, and an empty stdin (</dev/null, or a harness that closes stdin) also gives ''. guardedWrite then atomically replaces an existing file with an empty one and exits 0 with written:true. Reproduced: `echo important > home/rc; kit guarded-write --root home --file home/rc </dev/null` leaves rc at 0 bytes; the same under a pseudo-TTY (script -qc) creates a 0-byte file without waiting for input. Running the verb interactively, without a pipe, destroys the file's contents. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/guarded-fs.js:305.
fix_hint: In run(), refuse with exit 1 when io.stdinIsTTY is true. Also refuse empty content unless an explicit flag such as --allow-empty is given.

title: CLI stdin is decoded as UTF-8, so binary or non-UTF-8 content is corrupted
detail: cli.js readStdin returns Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf-8'), and run() passes that string to guardedWrite, which re-encodes it as UTF-8. Invalid bytes become U+FFFD. Reproduced: piping bytes ff fe 00 80 produced a 10-byte file (ef bf bd ef bf bd 00 ef bf bd), and the result still reported written:true. guardedWrite accepts a Buffer, but the stdin input path cannot deliver one.
fix_hint: Have the CLI pass the raw Buffer for guarded-write (for example an io.stdinBuffer(), or readStdin({ raw: true })) and hand it to guardedWrite unchanged.

title: Off Linux, a parent folder swapped after openParent sends the rename outside root, and the rollback then deletes the clobbered outside file
detail: When PROC is false (macOS and other non-Linux systems), base is the path res.parent, not the opened handle. If the folder is swapped for a link after openParent (the afterOpen window), the temp file is created and renamed through that link, replacing any same-named file outside root. The post-rename lstat goes through the same link, so the identity check passes. recheck() then refuses, and the rollback unlinks finalVia, which deletes the outside file. Reproduced with a copy of the module where PROC=false: outside/x containing 'PRECIOUS' was gone after guardedWrite threw KitExit 2. The header says a folder swapped after the walk is refused and nothing is written there, but off Linux a file outside the root is destroyed.
fix_hint: Off Linux, after creating the temp file and again just before rename, fstat the directory handle and compare it with lstat of the path; abort on any mismatch. Do not unlink in the rollback unless the parent path still resolves to the opened folder's dev+ino. If neither is possible, refuse to run when PROC is false.

title: push-gate header claims a walk from the home folder, confined to home, but the root is the receipts folder's real parent
detail: The header says store access is an 'identity-checked walk from the home folder' and that 'a dotfile link above it is followed while it stays under home'. storeFile() actually realpaths the receipts folder's parent (~/.claude/kit) and uses it as root, so a ~/.claude link that points anywhere, including outside home, is accepted. The new test 'a ~/.claude that links outside the home folder still stores receipts' asserts exactly that. The comment in the packaged test ('HOME is the root', test/kit-identity-checked-file-writes-packaged.test.js:31) repeats the error. A reader would assume a confinement to home that does not exist. The same text is in .claude/helpers/kit/push-gate.js.
fix_hint: Rewrite the header to say that links above the store are resolved without confinement, the root is the store's real parent, and only links inside the receipts folder are refused. Fix the packaged test comment to match.

title: guarded-write silently resets an existing file's permissions to 0600
detail: The temp file is created with mode 0600 (the default) and renamed over the target, so an existing file loses its original mode. Reproduced: a 0755 run.sh was 0600 after `kit guarded-write`, so its exec bit was gone. Neither the CLI usage nor the header mentions this.
fix_hint: When the final name already exists as a regular file, create the temp file with that file's mode, or document the 0600 reset in the usage text.

title: Dotfile-link push-gate test ends with a meaningless assertion and does not check the refused write left nothing behind
detail: assert.ok(f) only checks that a string is non-empty. After the refused receipt, the test never checks that receipts.real kept its original single JSON file and gained no temp or lock files, so a refusal that came after a partial write would still pass.
fix_hint: Replace assert.ok(f) with assertions that receipts.real still holds only the original JSON file with unchanged content, and no .tmp or .lock leftovers.

title: Post-rename 'undo' deletes the overwritten file: neither old nor new content survives
detail: When a check after the rename fails (the identity check at line 212 or recheck at line 213), the catch unlinks the file that was just renamed into place. On an overwrite the rename has already replaced the previous file, so removing it does not undo the write. It destroys the target completely. On Linux, finalVia is /proc/self/fd/<dir>/name, so the rename landed in the verified, opened folder, and the removal deletes a correctly placed file. Reproduced at HEAD 2245ccc. Pre-create d/x='OLD', then use an afterOpen hook that renames d to d-moved (a plain rename, as in the existing test). guardedWrite refuses with code 2 and d-moved/ ends up empty. Same with an afterRename hook that renames an ancestor folder with no symlink involved: a/b/f ends up gone. For push-gate this loses the whole receipt store (latest and previous). The header (line 26) and the error text ('the write was undone') say the opposite. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/guarded-fs.js.
fix_hint: Unlink only when the file may have landed outside the checked folder (the by-path case where `ours` was reached through a swapped link). In the /proc/self/fd case, leave the renamed file in place and just report the refusal. Alternatively, hard-link the old file aside before the rename and restore it on failure. Fix the header and the message to match, and add a test that pre-creates the target and asserts its content survives a refused write.

title: push-gate check now fails (exit 1) on a read-only or not-yet-created store location instead of answering
detail: storeFile() now runs fs.mkdir(parent, { recursive: true }) for every command, including the read-only `check`. When the store's parent does not exist and cannot be created (read-only HOME, a sandboxed or ro-mounted home, or a KIT_RECEIPTS_DIR pointing into a ro mount that does not exist yet), `check` throws KitExit 1 "cannot open the receipt store folder ..." instead of returning a decision. Reproduced: with HOME on a read-only tmpfs, the base commit (663025a) prints {decision: "ask", reason: "no review recorded ..."} with exit 0, while HEAD exits 1 with "cannot open the receipt store folder .../.claude/kit: ENOENT ... mkdir". It also means `check` now creates ~/.claude/kit as a side effect on every first run. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/push-gate.js:176. No test covers check against a missing or unwritable store location.
fix_hint: Only create the parent for `receipt` (pass a create flag to storeFile from run()); for `check`, if the parent does not exist, return null state (no receipt) without creating anything, e.g. realpath the deepest existing ancestor or treat ENOENT/EROFS from mkdir as 'no store yet'. Add a test that runs check with a HOME whose store parent is missing and cannot be created.

title: --diff: an added line starting with '++ ' is read as a file header and can abort the build
detail: diffPaths takes every line that starts with '+++ ' as a target path without tracking file/hunk state. An added line whose content begins with '++ ' (diff line '+++ ...') becomes a changed path. Reproduced: a markdown file gains the line '++ ../outside'; `git diff --no-prefix > d; cli.js graph --diff d` exits 1 with 'changed file "../outside" is not a path inside the repository', so the documented /w-review step fails on a valid diff. With other content the bogus path is silently added to `changed` and inflates `changed.requested`. Same code in .claude/helpers/kit/graph.js.
fix_hint: Only accept '+++ ' as a header when it directly follows a '--- ' line outside a hunk (or reset on 'diff --git'/'@@' as lenses.js parseDiff does); reuse lenses' parser.

title: --diff: quoted (non-ASCII or special-character) paths are dropped with no trace
detail: With git's default core.quotePath, a changed file such as src/café.js appears as '+++ "src/caf\303\251.js"'. diffPaths skips it, so the file is neither prioritised nor counted: reproduced output is changed {requested: 0, read: 0}, partial false, nothing in not_read. The review step is told to report what was not read, but this changed file vanishes silently, and under a budget/parse cut it may not be read at all.
fix_hint: Unquote C-style quoted paths (octal and \" \\ \t \n escapes, decode bytes as UTF-8), or at least record the dropped header so `changed` and `not_read` show it.

title: --diff: prefix stripping guesses from the filesystem and misses mnemonic prefixes
detail: The b/ prefix is removed only when '<top>/b/<path>' does not exist, and no other prefix is known. Reproduced: (1) repo with a top-level b/ folder holding a.js plus a root a.js; plain `git diff` of a.js gives '+++ b/a.js', and the graph marks b/a.js as the changed file instead of a.js. (2) with diff.mnemonicPrefix=true the header is '+++ w/src/a.js'; it is kept as-is, counted only in stats.missing, and the summary shows changed read 0 with no not_read entry. lenses.js in the same kit already parses the 'diff --git' header and handles a/ b/ i/ w/ c/ o/.
fix_hint: Derive the prefix from the 'diff --git'/'--- ' headers (reuse lenses.js parseGitHeader) instead of probing the filesystem.

title: --changed paths resolve against the repo top, not the cwd, unlike --dir and --diff
detail: --dir and a --diff file are resolved against the current directory, but --changed values are taken as repo-root-relative. Running `cli.js graph --changed a.js` from src/ (meaning src/a.js) reports changed {requested: 1, read: 0} and the real file is not prioritised. The usage text does not say which base is used.
fix_hint: Resolve --changed values against cwd and make them relative to the repo top, or state in usage that they are repo-root-relative.

title: validFacts does not bounds-check def/call indices, so a corrupt cache entry crashes every later build
detail: validFacts checks only that defs[].up and calls[].owner are integers. resolveGraph then dereferences them: facts.defs[u].up at line 999 and fi.nodes[owner].id at line 1128. Reproduced: run graph once in a small repo, change calls[0].owner to 7 (or defs[0].up to 9) in a cache file while keeping v and key, then run graph again. It exits 1 with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')' (or 'reading 'name''). The entry is never replaced, so every later run crashes the same way until someone deletes the cache by hand. The header promises that a cache file 'of the wrong shape is a miss, never trusted'.
fix_hint: In validFacts, require -1 <= d.up < k for each def (it must point to an earlier def) and -1 <= c.owner < defs.length for each call; anything else is a miss.

title: One refused cache entry turns the cache off for the whole run, and for every later run
detail: cacheGet calls cacheFail (cacheOn = false) on any code-2 refusal of a single entry, not only when the cache folder itself is refused. Two ways to trigger it. (a) Size mismatch: entries are written with guardedWrite's 64 MiB limit but read with maxCacheBytes (16 MiB). Reproduced with a 1 MB source of 'a()()' lines (inside maxFileBytes): its entry is 23 MB, is written on the first run, and is refused on every run after. (b) A single symlinked entry file. In both cases cache_hits drops to 0 for every file scanned after it. With --max-parses 1 the other files land in not_read as parse_cap and partial becomes true, even though their facts are cached. The bad entry is never rewritten, because cachePut is skipped once the cache is off.
fix_hint: In cacheGet, treat a refusal of one entry file as a miss and keep the cache on; call cacheFail only for a folder-level refusal. Also cap cachePut at o.maxCacheBytes (pass maxBytes to guardedWrite) so the cache never writes an entry it will refuse to read.

title: normalizeRel on git's own file list fails the whole build on a 'c:' name and silently drops names with backslashes
detail: buildGraph runs normalizeRel on every path from git ls-files (line 874), not only on paths the user gave. On Linux, a legal top-level file such as 'c:notes.txt' (any extension, even one that is not source) matches /^[A-Za-z]:/, and the verb exits 1 with 'is not a path inside the repository' (reproduced). A file named 'src/we\ird.js' is rewritten to 'src/we/ird.js', which does not exist. It is counted only in stats.missing and is not listed in not_read, and the result says partial:false while a source file was never read (reproduced).
fix_hint: Use git's -z output as-is (it is already top-relative POSIX). Apply the drive-letter and backslash handling only to user-supplied --changed paths. Alternatively, put a path that cannot be normalised in not_read with a reason instead of throwing or rewriting it.

title: cache_error is cut to 200 characters, so the reason is lost behind the long absolute path
detail: guardedRead/guardedWrite messages start with the full absolute cache-file path, a 64-character hash plus the repo path. slice(0, 200) leaves only that path. Reproduced: cache_error ended in '...cd01c3...f995.json is l' and '...json is a', so the reader cannot tell whether the cause was a size limit, a symlink or something else.
fix_hint: Store the reason separately from the path (for example a code plus the basename), or cut from the start of the message rather than the end.

title: changed.requested counts changed files that are not source, so read < requested looks like a gap
detail: requested is the size of the set of all changed paths, which includes .md, .json and similar files. read counts only parsed source files. Reproduced: a diff touching 4 JS files and 1 non-source file reports requested 5, read 4, and nothing in not_read explains the difference. w-review.md describes 'changed' as how many of the changed files were read, so a reviewer will look for a missing file that was never a candidate.
fix_hint: Count requested over changed files that are source files (sourceSet), or report a separate ignored count.

title: Sparse-checkout files are silently skipped and the graph still reports partial: false
detail: listRepoFiles uses `git ls-files --cached`, which lists skip-worktree entries that a sparse checkout (common in large repos and partial clones on slow links) never writes to disk. buildGraph treats each one as a deleted file (`e.missing` -> stats.missing++, continue): it is not added to not_read, so `partial` stays false. Repro: a repo with src/a.js (a) and lib/b.js (calls a), `git sparse-checkout set src`, then `cli.js graph --changed src/a.js` gives partial:false, not_read:[], stats.missing:1. lib/b.js is never read, and the result claims to be complete. The w-review step then allows 'nothing else calls a', which is exactly what the partial flag exists to prevent. The same applies to .claude/helpers/kit/graph.js.
fix_hint: List the files with `git ls-files -t` (or check the skip-worktree bit) and put skip-worktree entries in not_read with a reason such as 'not_checked_out', so partial becomes true. Keep genuinely deleted working-tree files counted as missing.

title: Fact cache is written at the git top without ignoring itself, so it shows up untracked outside the installer's .gitignore rule
detail: The cache goes to <git top>/.claude/kit/cache/graph. The only ignore rule is the one kit.js install appends to <targetDir>/.gitignore. When the suite is installed into a subfolder of a repository, that rule is anchored to the subfolder and does not cover the top-level cache. A run with --dir against a repository installed by an older kit has no rule at all. Repro: repo/app/.gitignore holds `.claude/kit/cache/`, then `cd app && cli.js graph` makes `git status -uall` show `?? ../.claude/kit/cache/graph/<sha>.json`. Those files can be committed by `git add -A`, and a top-level run of the w-review untracked-file loop puts every one of them into the review diff.
fix_hint: When the cache folder is created, also write a `.gitignore` containing `*` inside .claude/kit/cache/ (through guardedWrite), so the cache ignores itself wherever it lands.

title: CR-only line endings make the rest of the file a comment, so the facts are empty and get cached
detail: Line comments (and the shebang skip at line 108) end only at '\n', and line counting uses only '\n'. A file with old-Mac/CR-only line endings, which JavaScript accepts as line terminators, is consumed from its first `//` to the end of the file. extractFacts('// h\rexport function a(){ b(); }\rfunction b(){}\r', {path:'x.js'}) returns no defs, calls or exports, with no parse_error. This empty result is cached as if it were correct and is not listed in not_read.
fix_hint: Treat \r, U+2028 and U+2029 as line terminators: end // comments at any of them and count a lone \r (not followed by \n) as a new line.

title: Budget and per-file time limit use the wall clock (Date.now), which can step
detail: The default clock is Date.now, which is used for both the build budget and the per-file deadline (line 250). On VMs or older hosts where NTP steps the clock, a backwards step stops the budget and the per-file limit from firing, so a pathological file or a large tree can run past --budget-ms. A forward step cuts the build at once and marks files 'budget'.
fix_hint: Default the clock to performance.now (monotonic). It is a drop-in replacement for the clock option.
